title: Blackboard MVP (M0+M1): core-logic kernel, a Bb editor sort, and documentation slides
body:
## Blackboard MVP: a proof assistant's core logic inside Hazel

An experiment: an MVP of **Blackboard**, a proposed "clean slate" proof assistant whose core logic has a type of all types, an internal typing relation, and no lambda. Two milestones are here.

**Try it:** Documentation → Blackboard → 0. Overview, at https://hazel.org/build/blackboard-mvp/

### M0 — the kernel

`src/language/blackboard/` — `BbTerm` (terms `x`, `t : T`, `type`, `(x : T₁) → T₂`, `t₁ t₂`; signatures, blocks, documents; substitution, α-equivalence, printing), `BbCheck` (the decidable fragment the paper calls `tychk`, without conversion), `BbError` (errors as data, located by signature entry), `BbParse` (the paper's concrete syntax, for fixtures). No dependency on tiles or the web layer.

Tests use the paper's own signatures as fixtures. The checker finds the paper's two slips in `cong-ap` (a name bound twice; a family used as a type) and the two in `int-elim` (missing arguments), and records where the paper's examples lean on equations the fragment cannot use.

### M1 — the editor sort

`Bb(BbSort.Term)` is a nested sort, following the ALFA derivation sub-language in `src/language/derivation/`: forms in `Form.re`, molding, `MakeTerm`, a pretty printer, and `blackboard ... end` to embed a document in an expression. `BbGrammar` / `BbTermBase` / `Bb` carry editor terms and read them back as kernel terms, entries, blocks and documents. Statics and the cursor inspector are M2, so an embedded document is inert for now.

Two decisions worth review:

- **The colon binds tighter than the arrow**, so `(x : A) -> x : B` reads as the paper writes it. In a signature entry the colon is a declaration instead, and is loosest; `Bb.rotate_entry` rotates the spine back, so `f : A -> B` declares `f` of type `A -> B`.
- **`Insert.effective_sort` no longer falls back to the enclosing sort inside Blackboard.** It is a closed sub-language, so a token with no Blackboard expansion stays a monotile. Without this, typing `type` inside a block expands into Hazel's `type _ = _ in`. This is the one change outside Blackboard-specific code that affects existing behaviour; it is guarded by `Sort.is_bb`.

### Documentation slides

Five slides under **Documentation → Blackboard**: Overview, Terms, Signatures, Checking, Metatheory. They load through the typing parser, since menhir has no Blackboard productions (as with the derivation sub-language). Both corpus ratchets ledger them with a reason, and `DocSlides.ReparseBackuptext` pins their text fidelity.

The `Bb` sort also needed a colour: with no entry in the token palette, Blackboard code rendered in the fallback colour and was effectively unreadable. Measured against the code background, it is now 6.49:1, where `Exp` is 5.33, `Typ` 4.19, `Drv` 3.73 and `Pat` 3.32.

`Test_BlackboardSlides` requires every shipped slide to read back as a document. It earns its place: three separate content bugs made part of a slide silently become a hole while the text still round-tripped. Hazel names cannot contain a hyphen, so `falsity-eq` was three tokens; `false` is a boolean literal, not a name; and `witness : a : A` associates as `(witness : a) : A`. Slides therefore use underscores where the paper uses hyphens, noted on the Terms slide. Behind two of them was a reader bug: a signature of three or more entries nests to the right, and only the top level was being read.

### `mech/`

The Rocq mechanization of the core logic (`Blackboard.v`, Rocq 9.2, no axioms) and its compile log, as the reference semantics: consistency of the bare logic, conservativity of construction blocks, and a five-point model. It covers both the rules as first printed and the author's corrected `arrow+`. Not part of the build.

### Testing

```
dune build test/idb_stub.js test/haz3ltest.bc.js --profile dev
bash test/run_node.sh test Blackboard
```

23 Blackboard tests pass. The full suite was run: the only failure was `Evaluator and stepper are consistent`, which is the known QCheck flake — it passed on three consecutive re-runs.

### Not in this PR

Implicit arguments, user-defined syntax, tactics, equational rewriting, Blackboard statics in the editor, and menhir support.

title: Add dynamic mode to type projector
body: # Add dynamic mode to type projector Adds a **Dynamic** mode to the type projector, alongside Expected and Self. It infers the type of the values that actually flowed through an expression at runtime, and colours the parts of that type runtime supplied rather than statics. ## How it works **Inferring the type.** `DynamicTypInfer` runs statics over each of a probe's sample values in the program's context and meets the results. It returns an `option`, so a set of samples with inconsistent types is distinguishable from success. **Deciding what turns green.** Only the components runtime supplied go green, not the whole type. Given `(fun x -> ^^statics((1, x)))(true)`, statics knows `(Int, ?)` and runtime says `(Int, Bool)`, so `Bool` is green and `Int` stays the ordinary type colour. `Typ.diff` decides this by walking the two types together and returning the ids in the dynamic one that the static one does not account for. Two things make that harder than it sounds: - *The comparison has to run on the types as they will be laid out, not as they arrive.* Rendering first normalizes a type — desugaring `Sig`, inserting defensive parens as real nodes, padding out id slots — and those added nodes carry tokens of their own. Diffing the types as the caller passed them cannot name their ids, which is why parentheses inside a wholly runtime-derived type used to render in the static colour. Both types now go through `ExpToSegment.normalize_typ` first. It is not idempotent, so the normalized type is rendered once and handed back together with the ids to colour, rather than re-rendered later. - *Statics builds types with `Typ.temp`,* which stamps every node with the same `Id.invalid` sentinel. Left in, the whole set of ids collapses onto whichever tile the renderer emits first — which on a partially-known type means turning a component statics supplied green instead. The sentinels are replaced at the point where a type's ids become the ids of rendered tokens. `Typ.diff` also expands type aliases through `~ctx` to decide whether they differ, but returns the alias token's own id rather than the expansion's, since an alias renders as a single token. It terminates on cyclic alias chains. Sums get fine-grained diffing via `ConstructorMap.venn_regions`, falling back to colouring the whole dynamic Sum when the static type has constructors it lacks. **What you see.** The tiles named by that id set get a `dynamic` class, threaded through `ProjectorView` and `Code.re` as a `~classes` callback, and `proj-type.css` renders those green. **Probes under nested ascriptions.** In `3 : Int : Int` the two ascriptions are consistent, so the transition meets them and rewrites to a single `3 : Int` — and the inner `3 : Int` node is gone. A probe sitting on that node goes with it. That rewrite *is* the node's evaluation step, so there is no other point at which the probe could have observed its value, and on dev the ascription transition emits no side effects (`Transition.re`: `side_effects: []`), so nothing is recorded and the probe reports nothing. That matters for a feature whose only input is probe samples. Ascription transitions now collect the value through a writer monad in `Ascriptions.re` and report it as a `RecordAscriptionProbe` side effect, so `^^probe(3 : Int) : Int` records `3`. Pattern matching deliberately opts out with `Sample.no_targets`: the scrutinee is already final there, so its probes fired at the stack evaluation actually passed through, and collecting again would double-count. ## Testing - `Test_DynamicTypInfer.re` — inference from probe samples (basic types, meet behaviour, inconsistent samples, user-defined ADTs, unevaluated branches), and colouring driven through the same composition the projector runs. - `Test_DynamicTypIds.re` — properties tying the green ids to the render: every dynamic id is actually emitted, a wholly runtime-derived type has every tile green, a type runtime merely confirmed has none, and a normalized type already carries every id its rendering consumes. - `Test_DynamicTyp.re` — end-to-end dynamic type rendering. - `Test_Typ.re` — `Typ.diff` unit cases and the identity property. ## Notes The projector is not offered on type positions: `Info.typ` carries no expected or self type and types are not evaluated, so every mode would render `?`.

title: Hypothetical integration: Modules II parts 1-2 + hazel-html + livelits, with the HTML substrate as opt-in modules
body:
**Draft, for inspection only. Not meant to merge:** this branch is a hypothetical integration built to answer one question, and it contains merges of four other open PRs.

## What this is

dev + Modules II parts 1 and 2 (#2493 signature types and module values, #2494 width subtyping) + the HTML substrate (#2115) + the livelit stack (#2411 user-defined livelits, #2488 expansion typing, #2489 error dedup), with two follow-ups on top:

1. **The livelit code ported to real modules.** A livelit definition's `Model`, `Action` and `Expansion` are read as manifest type members of the signature `ModuleHelpers.module_sig_type` synthesizes; the livelit branch's own `collect_type_exports` and its labeled-tuple type-export injection in the `Let` case are gone. At runtime `LivelitProj.record_field` reads `ModVal` bindings by name from the evaluated `Module`. Two small changes; they are what user-livelits will need once Modules II lands.

2. **Prototype: the HTML substrate as opt-in modules.** hazel-html's ~120 global constructor names and seven global type aliases (`HTML`, `Attr`, `Cmd`, `Sub`, `App`, `KeyEvent`, `MouseEvent`) become four builtin module values `Html`, `Attr`, `Cmd`, `Sub` (`BuiltinsADT.HtmlModules`). Members are the constructors as snake_case functions, types are `Html.T`, `Attr.T`, `Cmd.T`, `Sub.T`, `Html.App`, `Attr.KeyEvent`, `Attr.MouseEvent`:

   ```
   Html.div([Attr.style([("color", "red")])], [Html.text("hi")])
   let view = fun m : Model -> ... : Html.T
   ```

   Constructor names are unchanged, so the renderer and MVU runtime are untouched. Motivation: a user module named `App` lost its type members to the builtin alias `App`, because `Typ.path_sig` tries type aliases before variables. With the modules it works.

## Performance

The naive module version was 3-4x slower than the global one. Four fixes, each at its source, bring it within ~15%:

- `sig_project_value` / `sig_project_type` substitute into the requested member only, instead of closing the whole signature to read one member.
- For a builtin module, a member's type keeps `T` as the path `Html.T` (`Typ.sig_project_value_along`), and `meet` accepts two equal paths without normalizing either.
- `normalize_ctr_type` keeps a builtin-module path compact, as it kept `Var("HTML")`.
- A builtin module's member elaborates directly to the constructor it denotes; otherwise the evaluator substitutes the whole module value into every closure that names `Html` (80 copies in one program's output).

| nutrient-rotation.hz | baseline (global names) | naive modules | final |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli analyze` | 2.3 s | 8.1 s | 2.8 s |
| `cli run` | 2.75 s | 11 s | 3.1 s |
| printed output | 181 KB | 1.3 MB | 181 KB |

## Verified

- All 14 MVU and livelit example programs type-check in the qualified form (ported, along with the docs, `Test_MVU` and `Test_UserLivelits`).
- 1370 tests across MVU, UserLivelits, Modules, Statics, Evaluator, Equality, Elaboration, Menhir, FastParse, Unicode pass. The three tests pinning the compact `Var("HTML")` annotation are removed: that fast path applied only to global aliases.
- In the browser: the MVU counter renders and counts on clicks, the slider livelit renders and updates with its expansion type check passing, and the Modules slide's item 9 (module named `App`) no longer errors.

## Known gaps

- The projectors doc slide reports type errors around the builtin `^^sliderf` and `^^text` livelits; those lines were not touched here and the errors predate the prototype (they belong to the merge, not the modules design).
- Bare `Int(x)` still type-checks because JSON's constructor `Int` is still global, so a missed port is silent. Same collision in miniature.
- Path-preserving projection and constructor elaboration apply only to builtin modules (variables with `Id.invalid`); user modules keep Modules II's manifest substitution.

title: Ascription steps make evaluation quadratic in call-stack depth (regression in Probes IV)
body:
## Summary

An ascription evaluated inside a recursive call now does work proportional to the current call-stack depth. A linear program becomes quadratic, and past roughly 10k frames it dies with a JS heap OOM rather than merely running slowly. This regressed in Probes IV (#2363) — dev immediately before that merge is linear.

## Repro

```hazel
let sum : Int -> Int =
  fun n -> if n == 0 then 0 else n + (sum(n - 1) : ?) in
sum(12800)
```

`./hazel run`, wall clock, baseline startup ~1.1s:

| n | `ac4df9feef` (before Probes IV) | `a816823aee` (Probes IV) |
|---|---|---|
| 3200 | 1.20 | 1.50 |
| 6400 | 1.29 | 2.62 |
| 12800 | 1.49 | **OOM** |
| 25600 | 2.04 | **OOM** |

OOM is `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit — JavaScript heap out of memory`. Every pre-merge run completes with the correct answer.

Delete the `: ?` and dev is linear again — 1.21 / 1.29 / 1.47 at 3200 / 6400 / 12800 — so it's the ascription, not the recursion.

## Cause

`Evaluator.re:246`, in the delegation bookkeeping Probes IV introduced:

```reason
(DHExp.rep_id(exp), CallStack.ids_of_stack(call_stack)),
```

`ids_of_stack` is `List.map((f: frame) => f.id, cs)` (`CallStack.re:29`) — O(stack depth), allocating a fresh list. It runs on every step whose kind is `may_delegate: true`, and per `Transition.re:186–188` those are exactly `Ascription`, `AscriptionTypAp` and `AscriptionAp`. One ascription step per frame at depth N gives Θ(N²) work, and since the entries are retained in `delegations`, Θ(N²) live memory — which is what actually kills it.

Counting the steps and summing the stack depth at each confirms the shape: 2000 steps → 1,997,003; 4000 → 7,994,003; 6000 → 17,991,003, i.e. k²/2.

Patching out only that `ids_of_stack` call restores linearity exactly: 1.23 / 1.32 / 1.52 / 2.02 at 3200 → 25600.

## Possible fixes

1. **Gate the insert on the redex id being a probe target.** The list is only consulted inside the `Some` branch of `switch (is_target)` at `Evaluator.re:298–302`, so an entry whose id isn't a target can never match. Semantics-preserving, and makes every unprobed program free. It does not fix a probed ascription inside deep recursion.
2. **Replace the materialized id list with a cheaper stack identity** — an incrementally maintained fingerprint, or keying on the stack value itself. This fixes it in general.

## Notes

Measured via the CLI on two worktrees at the commits above; the evaluator is untouched by any branch involved. `delegations` / `ids_of_stack` do not exist pre-merge (0 occurrences in `Evaluator.re` vs 26 after).

title: test: turn the stats-only statics surveys into disabled property tests
body:
The three `Slow` cases in Test_Statics_Properties.re counted how often a property held and printed a distribution. None of them asserted, so a regression in any of the three was invisible.

Each is now a real QCheck property wrapped in the `Alcotest.skip()` shape already used for `Preservation of types (disabled)` in Test_Evaluator_Properties.re, so the code stays compiled and re-enabling is a one-line edit.

All three properties are false. `Elaboration preserves type` was the surprise: its survey reported 1000/1000, but the survey seeded `Random.State.make([|0xC0FFEE|])`, and QCHECK_SEED=1 fails. The other two shrink to `(()) +. - []` (parent Float, fresh Int) and `{}`.

Dropped with the survey loops: two hand-rolled shrinkers that duplicated each other and QCheck's own shrinking, the outcome variants the loops tallied, and `show_exp`, which was a verbatim copy of QCheck_Util.show_core_exp.

`show_core_typ` moves out of `arb_typ` to a top-level let beside `show_core_exp`. Typ.show prints the whole IdTagged record, which rendered a type disagreement as two ten-line blobs rather than Float vs Int.

title: Live typing
body:
# Live typing

Adds a toggleable in-editor type feedback mode that fills in statically unknown types from what actually happened at runtime. Where a type is statically unknown, statics has nothing to check against and stays quiet; once runtime fills the unknown in, a genuine misuse becomes reportable.

Stacked on #1858, which contributes the machinery for colouring the runtime-derived parts of a type.

## Example

[Screencast From 2025-11-18 13-45-45.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42d6e2c5-e0f2-4093-b1ef-547807dc26d0)

## Probe selection

Integrated with the `Probe` pinning system, so you can get dynamic types for one particular function application by pinning it.

[Screencast From 2025-11-18 13-53-21.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d9bdec4-12d6-47d8-8fa3-d906989b9bc8)

## What you see

- Live-typing errors get their own decoration in the editor — a pulsing dashed outline in a colour distinct from ordinary static errors — so it is clear that an error depends on runtime information.
- The cursor inspector shows the refined type with the runtime-derived components in green, and a ⚡ badge in its header when only the dynamic info reports an error.
- They also collect in the problem panel under a `LiveTyping` category.

## Implementation

- **Probing what statics could not resolve** — with `live_typing` on, `CachedStatics.compute_targets` unions `ids_with_unknown_types(info_map)` into the probe targets, so every expression and pattern whose `elab_syn_ty` still contains an unknown gets sampled. The feature supplies its own inputs rather than depending on where you happened to place probes.
- **`LiveTyping.re`** — carries per-expression dynamic samples and per-TPat type instantiations, consumed by `Statics.mk(~dynamics=...)`. A term's samples are only consulted when its type actually has unknowns to fill.
- **`CodeWithStatics.re`** — filters `Dynamics.t` by the current `sample_focus` and runs statics a second time with the dynamic info, surfacing dynamic-only errors as `live_typing_error_ids`. The second pass is throttled during streaming evaluation.
- **`Dynamics.TypeInstMap` / `EvaluatorState.RecordTypeInstantiation`** — TypAp transitions record the concrete type at each type-variable instantiation, so polymorphic code gets instantiation-aware feedback instead of a spurious error on the parameter. `(typfun a -> fun x : a -> x)@<String>("")` no longer reports on `x`.
- **`Typ.join` / `join_all`** — the lattice dual of `meet`, used by `LiveTyping.extend_ctx_with_instantiations` to combine the observed instantiations of a type variable. Like `meet`, it hands back the alias when the join does not refine it, and it stops rather than looping on a cyclic alias chain.
- **Closure scoping** — `DynamicTypInfer.type_of_sample` substitutes a sampled closure's own environment before typing it. Statics discards a closure's env, so the body's free variables would otherwise resolve against the probe site's context and capture whatever same-named binder happens to be in scope there.
- **Cursor inspector** — `CursorInspector.view_type` takes `~live_typing_info` and, where the dynamic type differs from the static one, renders the segment and green ids that `DynamicTypInfer.segment_and_dynamic_ids` returns.
- **Settings** — `CoreSettings.live_typing`, off by default, toggled from the nut menu with a performance warning.

## Testing

`test/evaluator/Test_Evaluator_LiveTyping.re` covers the end-to-end flow: sample collection, meet across samples, pinned-call filtering, and polymorphic instantiation.

`Test_Typ.re` covers `Typ.join` — equal atoms, Unknown, sums, unbound variables, alias preservation, cyclic-alias termination. `Test_DynamicTypInfer.re` adds a closure-scoping case, and a check that a type built the way statics builds them colours only its runtime-derived components.

## Known limitations

- `DynamicTypInfer` runs a full `Statics.mk` per sample with no memoization. Tolerable for a single projector in Dynamic mode, more of a concern here, where live typing needs dynamic types for many expressions at once.

title: CI: weekly Extended Tests, and test reports on the test job
body:
Two changes to how CI reports, and how far it searches.

**Weekly Extended Tests.** New `.github/workflows/extended-tests.yml` runs Sundays against `dev` (plus `workflow_dispatch` with `factor`/`seed`), calling a new `make ci-extended`: the whole suite with `QCHECK_LONG=1`, so every QCheck `~count` is multiplied by `QCHECK_LONG_FACTOR`. Per-push CI runs each property once, so a property that fails on one seed in a few hundred never surfaces. The job pins its seed and writes the reproducing `QCHECK_*` command to its summary. It gates nothing — a red run is a bug report.

The default factor is 100 because `Slow` turns out not to mean `QCheck`: 237 tests carry the tag, only 12 are properties, so the factor scales a minority of the run and the rest is a fixed floor. That puts it at roughly 3.7 h on CI against GitHub's 6 h cap. Correct it from the first real run.

**Test reports move off the Deploy job.** `checks.yml` passed `use-actions-summary: false` to `dorny/test-reporter@v1`, but that input doesn't exist until v2 — it was ignored and a check run was always created. GitHub picks which of a commit's check suites a check run joins, and it picked Deploy's, so test results rendered under `Deploy branch preview` and a red suite made the deploy look broken. On `@v3` the default writes the report to the running job's summary and creates no check run, which is the only placement we control.

The table now appears on the `Fast checks` / `Full tests` summaries; the `Test Report` and `Quick Test Report` rows and their inline annotations go away. Nothing is lost as a gate — those jobs already fail on a red suite, and the report checks could never have been required, since fork PRs skip them. Consequently `checks: write` is gone, and `publish-reports` (which now only gated Codecov) is renamed `upload-coverage`, with fork PRs getting their reports too.

Comments in these files lost their measured numbers in favour of the reasoning and how to re-measure — the `~32-min suite` note was already wrong at 18, and the `~92%` beside it is what made factor 8 look like four hours.

**Verifying.** This PR's CI run should show the results table under Fast checks and Full tests, with no report rows under Deploy. `extended-tests.yml` can't run until it's on `dev`; after merge, `gh workflow run "Extended Tests" --ref dev -f factor=1` smoke-tests it in a couple of minutes.

title: Rich probe: exiting drawer mode leaves the renderer active with nothing rendered ("Hide table" on a table that isn't shown)
body:
Regression since #2363.

### Repro

1. Probe an expression whose value is a list of tuples with 4+ rows.
2. Right-click the sample → **View as table**. The table needs more than `inline_rows_cap = 4` rows, so it can't embed in the sample chip; activation implicitly opens the drawer and the table renders between the lines.
3. Click the nav-bar chevron (`Toggle drawer (⌘↓ / ⌘↑)`), or press ⌘↑ or Escape.
4. The sample reverts to abbreviated text — the table is gone from the screen.
5. Right-click the sample again: the menu still reads **`Hide table`**, not `View as table`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d55f92a6-d5eb-432c-b975-52ba7f065538

### Why

- `ToggleDrawerMode` / `SetDrawerMode(false)` flip only `drawer_mode`; `active_renderer` stays `Some(table)` (`ProbeProj.re:2294-2309`).
- Offsides, a rich view embeds in the chip only when `drawer_rows <= inline_rows_cap` (`ProbeProj.re:772-787`, cap at `:361`), and for a table `drawer_rows = List.length(rows) + 1` (`TableRenderer.re:51`). The anchored modal that used to host it is retired (`let modal_nodes = [];`, `ProbeProj.re:2489-2492`). So there is nowhere left for it to render.
- The menu label is keyed on the model alone, not on whether anything is on screen:

```reason
let is_active = ctx.active_renderer_id == Some(r.id);
let label = (is_active ? "Hide " : "View as ") ++ r.id;   /* ProbeProj.re:1022-1025 */
```

### Effect

The label is wrong, and recovering the table takes two menu trips: `Hide table` (clears `active_renderer`) then `View as table` (recomputes `wants_drawer` and reopens the drawer).

### Suggested fix

Make the item a toggle over "is something actually rendered" rather than "is a renderer selected": either clear `active_renderer` when leaving the drawer if the renderer can't render inline, or derive `is_active` from the rendered surfaces and let a click on an already-selected renderer re-open the drawer.

### Adjacent, same predicate

`ToggleModal` ignores its payload whenever any renderer is already active (`ProbeProj.re:2351-2354`), so `View as card` while `table` is active just deactivates the table instead of switching renderers.

title: Rich table probe: the column (⋮) menu opens at the bottom of the drawer instead of under the column header
body:
Since #2363 — specifically `7428e0e88b`, which retired the anchored modal.

### Repro

Open a table rich probe in the drawer with few enough rows that the drawer doesn't scroll, then click a column's ⋮. The menu appears below the bottom edge of the table rather than under that column's header.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0dbcc198-08bf-4da4-bcd6-6a41198c4d60

### Why

- The `.cm-*` rules place the menu with `top: 100%; left: 0` and are documented as anchoring "inside the `<th>` cell" (`proj-table-probe.css:34-68`). Those offsets resolve against the nearest **positioned** ancestor.
- The only rule that ever made the `th` positioned is `.modal .table th { position: relative }` (`proj-table-probe.css:138-146`), and `.modal` is no longer rendered: `let modal_nodes = []; let _unused_modal = modal_overlay;` (`ProbeProj.re:2489-2492`).
- So the containing block is now `.below-wrapper .rich-drawer { position: relative }` (`proj-probe.css:822-824`) — and `top: 100%` is the bottom of the whole drawer.
- Corroboration: a **tall** table gets `.below-wrapper .rich-drawer.overflowing .table th { position: sticky }` (`proj-probe.css:844-847`), which does establish a containing block, so those tables place correctly. Only short / non-overflowing drawer tables are wrong.
- `Menu.direction_from_id` (`src/util/Menu.re:538-546`) measures the ⋮ button against `#main` and only picks a class name; placement is entirely CSS. The flip decision is honest; the anchor is wrong.

### Suggested fix

Give the header cell a containing block that doesn't depend on the retired modal — e.g. `.table th:has(> .column-menu) { position: relative }`, or hang it off the `menu-open` class the `th` already gets while its menu is open (`TableRenderer.re:433-441`). An unconditional `.table th { position: relative }` would fight the two `position: sticky` rules (`proj-probe.css:844`, `proj-table.css:63`).

### Cleanup that belongs with the fix

Retiring the modal left dead code behind, and that is what broke this anchor:

- `modal_overlay` is unreachable, kept alive only by `let _unused_modal = modal_overlay;` (`ProbeProj.re:2370-2414`, `:2489-2492`).
- The whole `.modal …` block in `proj-table-probe.css:80-169` is orphaned.
- The `nut-menu` class in the column menu's class list is inert — every `nut-menu.css` rule is scoped to `#top-bar`.

title: Projector `dynamics` flag has had no reader since the MakeTerm probe rework
body:
`Projector.dynamics: bool` (`ProjectorBase.re:209`, forwarded by `Cook` at `:271`) is documented as "this projector will be instrumented with a probe to collect dynamic information during evaluation", but nothing reads it.

It was added in 99b100f72f (2024-12-29, "projector API flag for dynamics collection") with a real consumer: `MakeTerm.should_instrument` looked it up to decide whether a probe-wrapped term actually received a `Probe` wrapper at parse time —

```reason
| (label, [Exp(body)]) when is_probe_wrap(label) =>
  ret(should_instrument(Exp.rep_id(body)) ? Parens(body, Probe(...)) : body.term)
```

That consumer was removed in 9a8cd47887 (2026-01-08, "rm legacy probe code in maketerm") and nothing replaced it. `ProjectorInfo.mk_info` now populates `info.dynamics` from the dynamics map regardless of the flag, so a projector's declared value has no effect either way.

Consequences: the declaration is misleading — someone tracing where a projector's samples come from is sent to a dead end, and setting it `true` on a new projector looks like opting in when it does nothing. Ten implementations plus the signature carry a value nobody consumes.

Either give it a consumer (if per-projector gating of sample collection is still wanted) or delete it from the signature, `Cook`, and the ten implementations. Removal touches 11 files for zero behaviour change, which is why it wants its own PR rather than riding along with feature work.

title: No probe (sample context) menu in drawer mode
body:
Since #2363 introduced drawer mode.

The sample context menu — pin, step into, `View as …` / `Hide …`, call display, environment — opens on right/alt-click of a sample chip (`.value`, `ProbeProj.re:723-750`). In the drawer that chip is not reachable, so the menu can't be opened for anything shown there.

### With a rich renderer active

The drawer content **replaces the sample views wholesale**:

```reason
switch (empty_status, rich_content) {
| (None, Some(content)) => [content]     /* ProbeProj.re:2054-2057 */
| (None, None) => ... sample_view ...
```

so there is no `.sample` / `.value` node in the drawer at all — no `on_contextmenu` (the repo has exactly two: `ProbeProj.re:718` and `CodeEditable.re:1087`) and no `sample-context-menu` node. A right-click over the table bubbles out — the projector wrapper deliberately passes right-clicks through (`ProjectorView.re:283-292`) — and opens the **editor** context menu, which has no `Hide table`.

### With plain samples in the drawer

Reported broken too. Here the chips *are* rendered (`~display=Block`) and the menu is meant to be promoted to a `FloatingElement` so `.below-wrapper`'s overflow can't clip it (`ProbeProj.re:1294-1309`, `proj-probe.css:1006-1011`) — so that promotion path needs checking as well.

### Why it matters

The context menu is the only place offering `Hide table` / `View as table`, so once a rich view is in the drawer the menu that would turn it off is unreachable from it. The only exits are the drawer's `×` — which exists only when `active_renderer != None`, so auto-rich drawers have none (`ProbeProj.re:2484`) — the nav-bar chevron, and ⌘↑/Escape, and none of those clear `active_renderer` (see #2519).

### Suggested direction

Give the drawer its own right-click surface that opens the indicated sample's context menu (the drawer already takes keyboard focus and knows the indicated sample, `ProbeProj.re:2040-2052`) instead of falling through to the editor menu.

title: Folder-style tutorial lessons
body:
Stacked on #2485. **All three PRs in this stack are meant to be merged together** — they are split for review only.

## Summary

Documentation mode already renders `/`-separated slide names as nested breadcrumb dropdowns (`"B2T2 / Table API / Constructors / vcat"`). Tutorial mode has 25 lessons in one flat list. This PR names that hierarchy and then gives tutorial mode folders on top of it.

### `SlidePath`

The hierarchy was an ad-hoc convention spread across three unrelated places: a local `split_filepath` plus inline `take`/`nth`/`dedup_f` in `EditorModeView.indicator_select`, ~60 hardcoded `" / "` literals in `src/b2t2/Slides.re` and `src/docslides/Slides.re`, and `"Derivations / " ++ spec.title` in `Init.re`.

`src/web/util/SlidePath.re` makes it a type:

```reason
type t = {
  folders: list(string),
  leaf: string,
};
```

and owns the operations both modes need: `of_string`/`to_string`, `folder`/`same_folder`, the folder-scoped index arithmetic the navigation arrows use (`folder_indices`, `folder_position`, and `step_in_folder`, which clamps), and `breadcrumb` — the sibling-dropdown decomposition lifted out of the view.

`indicator_select` is now a thin render over `breadcrumb` and takes `list(SlidePath.t)`, which dropped 69 lines from it along with two latent crashes it had been carrying:

- `List.nth(parts', prefix_depth)` raised `Failure("nth")` whenever one slide name was an exact proper prefix of another — a slide named `Tables` alongside `Tables / Tables` would have taken down the whole top bar. Such a path is now skipped, making it merely unreachable from the deeper dropdown.
- `Option.get` on the changed option's index lookup.

Slide names stay plain strings at the persistence boundary — they are IndexedDB keys (`"doc:" ++ name`) and `.hzt` `@title` text — so nothing about the stored format changes; callers convert at the view/navigation boundary.

### Tutorial folders

A lesson's `@title` is now a `SlidePath`, and both arrow surfaces — the in-slide prev/next pair and the top-bar arrows — **step within the current lesson's folder**, clamping at its edges, so the last lesson of a folder shows `Done! 🎉` instead of a next arrow. Crossing folders goes through the folder dropdown. The slide heading shows just the leaf, since the breadcrumb above it already names the folder.

| Folder | Lessons |
|---|---|
| `Basics` | 19 — Holes through Labeled Tuple Projection |
| `Tuple Structural Operations` | 3 — Extension, Omission, List Conversions |
| `Tables` | 6 — Tables, Table Column Projection, Rich Probes, and the three Gradebook tasks below |

Rich Probes sits under Tables because it is a rich probe *for* tables.

### Three tasks recovered from `tables-study`

`Tables` also picks up Gradebook Midterm Mean, Gradebook Overall Grade, and Gradebook Tidy Term — study tasks that had never been ported off the `tables-study` branch, where they were `Ta_*.ml` zipper dumps of 0.5–0.9 MB each. They keep their original ids, so they are the same lessons the study ran.

They were converted by adapting the dumps to the current types (the drift was two things per file: `selection` gained `anchor_caret`/`smart_rounded`, and `refractors` dropped `autos`/`sample_cursor` with `manuals` unchanged), compiling them in alongside `TaskRefDocs`, and running `./hazel tutorial-decode` — which also expanded each task's composed `TaskRefDocs` sections into a literal `@reference`. None of that scaffolding is in the tree.

Two content fixes on top of the decode: Midterm Mean's table held 20 literals like `85.000000`, and past six significant digits a slide falls onto the quadratic parser (slowness being the only symptom), so those are normalized to `85.0`; and its hidden tests did not round-trip, because an implicit `¿` hole collapses to nothing before a `,` inside a labeled tuple, so those twelve are now the explicit `?` token.

Not ported, deliberately: the two Bug Identification tasks, which depend on live typing; the 27 pre-placed probe refractors these three carried (`Triggers.refractor_seg_to_seg` only emits `^^probe(...)` for a refractor whose id is a term root in the current parse, and these ids came from the older grammar, so 26 of 27 dropped); and the study's `setting_overrides` condition flags and `?treatment` A/B ordering, none of which has a `.hzt` marker. The commit records what each task's flags were.

All three start as real tasks — a hole in Midterm Mean, an identity-stub `tidy_term` — so their hidden tests fail until solved.

Recategorizing is safe: lesson identity is the `id=<uuid>` flag introduced in #2485, not the title, so moving a lesson between folders does not reset anyone's saved progress.

`hazel-programs/tutorial/README.md` documents the authoring rules — one folder segment per lesson, no title a proper prefix of another, a folder's lessons contiguous in `src/tutorialslides/Slides.re`, and `Basics / Holes` first because it is the lesson a fresh profile opens on.

## Deliberately not done

A ✔ on a folder's dropdown option when the whole folder is complete. It cannot be built from current data: `TutorialsMode.Update.calculate` evaluates only the current lesson and `TutorialMode.Model.persist` saves only zippers, so `all_tests_passed` is `false` for every non-current lesson — which is also why today's per-lesson ✔ from `return_title` can only ever show for the lesson you are standing on. A real folder ✔ needs persisted per-lesson completion, which is its own change.

## Test plan

- [x] `make dev` builds clean, no new warnings
- [x] `make test-quick` — 3501/3501
- [x] `./hazel tutorial-verify` — 28/28 slides round-trip cleanly
- [x] `Test_SlidePath` (23 cases) — parsing, accessors, folder navigation, and breadcrumb, including the proper-prefix path that used to raise and an out-of-range index
- [x] `Test_Tutorial` (7 cases) — ratchets the authored lessons: folder set and sizes (`Basics x19`, `Tuple Structural Operations x3`, `Tables x6`), contiguity, `Basics / Holes` first as the default lesson, no title a proper prefix of another, and that repeated next/prev traverses exactly one folder and then stops
- [x] Documentation mode — `B2T2 / …` breadcrumbs and `Derivations / …` still render and switch slides
- [x] Tutorial mode — opens on `Basics / Holes`; arrows walk one folder and stop at its ends; the dropdown crosses folders

title: Author tutorial lessons as .hzt text
body:
Stacked on #2250, with #2513 on top. **All three PRs in this stack are meant to be merged together** — they are split for review only.

## Summary

Adopts the text-authored tutorial system from `probes-study-rebuilt` and converts all 25 lessons to it.

Each lesson used to be an `.ml` file holding a serialized zipper alongside its prose — ~26,000 lines of generated data that had to be regenerated by hand for any edit. Lessons are now plain-text `.hzt` files in `hazel-programs/tutorial/`, embedded with `ppx_blob` via a new `src/tutorialslides` library (a clone of `src/docslides`) and parsed into `Tutorial.spec` at startup by `TutorialText`:

```
@title      the lesson name
@flags      wrapper show_report version=N id=<uuid>
@prompt     markdown for the instructions panel
@hint       one-liner
@reference  markdown for the Task Reference sidebar
@hints      one per line
@code       editor contents (holes are ¿, or ? to survive a container)
@test       hidden tests
```

Net: **+2,855 / −26,285**.

The conversion was mechanical. `TutorialDecode` reads whatever lesson list is compiled in and emits `.hzt` via `MarkerParse.to_text`, so the CLI landed first and generated all 25 from the existing `Tu_*.ml`. `./hazel tutorial-verify` checks that each slide's impl and tests are a fixed point of `to_text ∘ of_text ∘ to_text`; all 25 are. `TaskRefDocs` is gone — decode inlines each lesson's composed `task_reference` into its own `@reference`.

One marker is ours rather than upstream's: **`@title`**. Upstream derives the title from the filename, which would renumber every lesson and mangle four of them (`Reverse Function Application (Pipelining)` losing its parens; `and`/`of` capitalising). `@title` pins the exact title and falls back to the derived one.

## Bugs the round-trip check surfaced

- **`$==` in the Case Expressions and Folding Lists hidden tests.** `$` does not lex in Hazel, so those six tests were unsatisfiable and always reported indeterminate — a live bug the serialized form hid. Now `==`, and both suites pass.
- **`[¿]` in List Literals** collapsed to `[]` on reparse, losing the fillable hole. Explicit `[?]` round-trips.
- Stray trailing grouts in five hidden-test cells.

## Tutorial-mode chrome

Also ports the styling/UX work from that branch:

- a collapsible **Tasks** section, split from the prompt at its `Task` header (all 25 lessons now have one)
- the hint as a keyed `<details>`, so its open state no longer leaks across slides
- first/last slide nav gating — **required**, since `.hzt` `version` defaults to 1 and the old `version > 1` / `version < 10` gates would break
- SAND background, focus-driven cell accent, `{{video:}}` and `{{no_editor}}` prompt markers
- per-slide scroll memory, and driving the slide `<select>` from the model so it follows keyboard navigation
- `Zipper.caret_to_start`, so `@code` loads with the caret at the start of the program

`show_report` changes meaning under the new `show_task_ui` gate — it now marks a slide as a *task* (grading face + report icon) rather than "start with the report panel expanded" — so it is set on the six converted lessons that have real hidden tests. Only Probes, whose sole test is `test true end`, leaves it off.

Four general CSS fixes come along: a broken pin-icon URL in `style.css` (which sits in `www/`, so `../img/` resolved outside it), the test sigil's `z-index` (it painted above projector overlays), `nowrap` on context-menu items, and overscroll containment so a nested horizontal scroll does not fire the browser back-gesture.

## Deliberately left behind

`TutorialProbeStrip` and `TutorialSlideInit` — both are exhaustive hardcoded tables over that branch's own slide ids and need `AutoProbe.t` plus new `ProbeProj.Settings` variants — and the probe/evaluator/Card rework they depend on.

- [x] `make test-quick` — 3465/3465
- [x] `./hazel tutorial-verify` — 25/25 slides round-trip cleanly
- [x] All 25 lessons in the dropdown, in order, with their exact original titles
- [x] Tables driven to 3/3 passing; Folding Lists to 3/3 (previously impossible)
- [x] Tasks + Hint collapsibles, grading face and panel, prev/next gating, Task Reference sidebar

title: Migrate src/language to Jane Street Core
body:
Migrates `src/language` to Jane Street Core. **Zero downstream edits** were needed.

Two commits, reviewable separately:

1. **`Make equality explicit at the type in src/language`** — 126 sites, no Core involved. Names the equality witness at each comparison (`String.equal`, `Id.equal`, `Bigint.equal`, or a `[@deriving eq]`-generated one). This lands standalone and is worth reading on its own.
2. **`Migrate src/language to Jane Street Core`** — the flip.

**Equality strategy.** `int` needs nothing (Core permits `=` there, ~92 sites). Concrete types name their witness. Whole-term structural comparison uses `Poly` — 26 explicit `Poly.equal` plus `open Poly` in the four modules whose *job* is structural comparison (`Equality`, `MatchExp`, `DrvTermBase`, `Operators`). `Typ.re` deliberately stays under Core's discipline with its sites fixed individually; it's where an accidental equality matters most.

**Traps worth knowing about for review.** Several stdlib functions have same-named *total* counterparts in Core, so the flip changes the return type rather than failing to compile — `List.hd`/`tl`/`nth`/`find` become options and only break at the use site. `IdTagged.rep_id = List.hd(ids)` silently became `Id.t option` and surfaced two modules away. All swept to `_exn`. `Float.modf` returns a record, not a tuple, and `BuiltinsBase.re` uses `Stdlib.ceil` etc. deliberately — those back Hazel's *language-level* float builtins, so they need to be exact rather than a plausible Core equivalent.

title: Delete Util.Either: result where it means success-or-failure, Core.Either where it means a partition
body:
Follows up [a review comment on #2439](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/pull/2439#discussion_r3830911397) asking whether `Either` isn't already built into OCaml. It is — twice — and ours was redundant, but the call sites turned out to want two different things.

## Why ours had to go

`src/util/Either.re` was four lines: `type t('l, 'r) = L('l) | R('r)` with `show`/`sexp`/`yojson`. Those derivations were dead — no `[@deriving]` type in the tree embeds an `Either.t`, which was the one plausible reason to keep our own over Core's.

It also **shadowed Core's**. Every library that uses it has `-open Core` in its dune, and every file that uses it also does `open Util`, which lands second, so `Core.Either` was unreachable without qualifying it.

## What the call sites actually wanted

Of 24 references, 20 were success-or-failure wearing the wrong constructors:

| Site | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `Operators.re` (13) | `Either.t(Atom.t, bad_literal)` | `result(Atom.t, bad_literal)` |
| `Atom.re` (3) | `Either.t('b, InvalidOperationError.t)` | `result('b, InvalidOperationError.t)` |
| `Transition.re` (4) | `Either.L(return_value)` / `Either.R(error)` | `Ok` / `Error` |
| `MatchedTyp.args` | `Either.t('a, int)` | `result(list(Typ.t), int)` |

`result` puts the error direction in the type instead of leaving it to a convention about which side `R` is, and `MatchedTyp.args` gets a concrete ok type rather than the `'a` it was carrying.

Only **`Aba.split`** and its single caller **`Segment.split_by_matching`** genuinely partition — each element goes to the A-stream or the B-stream, and neither side is an error. Those take `Core.Either`'s `First`/`Second`.

`src/util/Either.{re,rei}` and `Util`'s re-export of it are deleted. Removing the module made `open Util` dead in `MatchedTyp.re`, so that went too.

`BuiltinsADT`'s `Either` is the Hazel-language type alias — a different thing entirely — and is untouched.

## Verification

- `dune build @check --profile release` clean (no warnings)
- `make dev` clean
- `make test-quick`: 3556 tests pass

No behavior change is intended: this is a type-and-constructor rename, plus one type made less general.

title: Migrate src/haz3lcore to Jane Street Core
body:
Migrates `src/haz3lcore` to Jane Street Core — the last layer between `src/language` and `src/web`. Two commits: typed equality then the flip.

**Point-free re-export shims were the interesting failure mode.** `haz3lcore/lang/Token.re` aliases stdlib functions (`let concat = String.concat;`, `let sort_uniq = List.sort_uniq(compare);`). An alias silently inherits Core's argument order and labels, so every caller changes meaning without the alias itself failing to compile. Each one now has an explicit arity:

```reason
let concat = (sep, xs) => String.concat(~sep, xs);
let starts_with = (~prefix, s) => String.is_prefix(s, ~prefix);
```

**Operator sections** are the same hazard in miniature: `(==)(x)` is polymorphic equality partially applied. Six in this library, and they were not all strings — `Skel` compares a `Token.t list`, `Segment` a `Sort.t`.

Also worth noting for review: a `let compare = compare;` inside a comparator module was polymorphic under stdlib and becomes int-only under Core, which breaks the `Set.Make` it feeds. And `Core.Random.State.t` is not `Stdlib.Random.State.t` — QCheck wants the stdlib one, so seeded generators keep `Stdlib.Random`.

title: A lone ¿ inside a container is dropped by the text round-trip: [¿] reloads as []
body:
`MarkerParse.of_text` recovers Grout by *deleting* the `¿` marker tile and letting the load-time regrout put Grout back — `strip_implicit_holes` does `Select.tile` then `Destruct.go` ([`src/haz3lcore/zipper/MarkerParse.re:94-111`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/dev/src/haz3lcore/zipper/MarkerParse.re#L94-L111)). That only recovers a hole where regrout would independently place one, so a marker whose removal leaves a **complete** term is lost.

The reachable case is a hole as a container's sole element:

| authored | after one round-trip | |
|---|---|---|
| `[¿]` | `[]` | ✗ dropped |
| `[¿, 1]` | `[¿, 1]` | ✓ |
| `[1, ¿]` | `[1, ¿]` | ✓ |
| `(¿, 1)` | `(¿, 1)` | ✓ |
| `let x = ¿ in x` | `let x = ¿ in x` | ✓ |

Delete the marker in `[¿]` and `[]` is already a well-formed empty list, so regrout has no reason to insert anything.

This is a persistence bug, not just a notational one: grout inside `[]` is a state the editor reaches by typing — inserting a space in `[|]` gives `[ <>|]`, per example III of #1077 — and `to_text` prints it as `[¿]`, so the document does not survive a reload. Same shape as #2450 (a dangling `;` dropping every probe pin from the round-trip), which was fixed.

## Repro

Put `let xs : [Int] = [¿] in xs` in a tutorial lesson's `@code` and run `./hazel tutorial-verify --verbose`:

```
List Literals                      impl:MISMATCH  tests:OK
  --- impl before roundtrip ---
let xs : [Int] = [¿] in
xs
  --- impl after roundtrip ---
let xs : [Int] = [] in
xs
```

## Fix direction

Replace the marker tile with a Grout piece directly instead of destruct-then-regrout, so an authored hole is preserved wherever it was written rather than only where regrout independently agrees one belongs.

## Related

- **#2479** adds the right gate for this class — `TextRoundtrip.EditedGrout` requires grout to survive the load-time regrout and reprint as a fixed point — but its corpus is grout left by *simulated typing* and doesn't cover the sole-element case. It keeps the destruct mechanism and adds a second pass for `⧖`, so it does not fix this.
- **#2406** (grout-free edit state, holes as derived display cells) would obsolete the problem entirely.
- **#2455** is a third `¿` gap: markers inside projector syntax are never found or destructed.
- **#1077** documents that grout inside `[]`/`()` is reachable by typing.

title: Migrate src/util to Jane Street Core
body:
Migrates `src/util` to Jane Street Core. This is the first library in the migration and the minimum atomic step, since `-open Core` applies per dune library — every `.re` in the stanza has to compile at once.

**Wiring.** Adds `core` to `dune-project` and `(flags (:standard -open Core))` to the `util` library stanza, which inherits the centralised warning settings from `dune-workspace` via `:standard`. `core` and `base` are already transitive deps of `bonsai.web`, `bignum`, `virtual_dom` and `incr_dom`, so opening Core costs no extra bundle size.

Core's comparator-based sets have a different interface (`add(t, elt)` argument order, `length` not `cardinal`, comparator-carrying `empty`) and `src/language` / `src/haz3lcore` call the stdlib shape. They migrate later in this stack; converting the containers now would force churn in libraries this PR doesn't touch.

title: Add .rei interfaces for 13 leaf modules

Same mechanism as the previous PR, applied to leaf modules — ones with only one or
two callers. These had no interface, so every internal helper was exported to all
485 modules in the build. Declaring just the surface used across files removes
**267 values from the public API for 24 declarations**, in 213 lines.

The public set came from the `ocaml-index` occurrence data — a value is public iff
some occurrence lies in another file — not from grep, so it is the same data
`scripts/find_dead_code.py` already reasons about.

| module | now private | declared |
|---|--:|--:|
| `DebugSidebar` | 47 | 1 |
| `TyDiForms` | 35 | 3 |
| `ContextMenu` | 31 | 3 |
| `CursorInspector` | 30 | 5 |
| `Abbreviate` | 27 | 2 |
| `CustomStatics` | 24 | 2 |
| `SampleFocusBar` | 16 | 1 |
| `Sidebar` | 14 | 1 |
| `SlashCommandOutputView` | 12 | 1 |
| `CompositionPrompt` | 11 | 1 |
| `WorkerMessagingSection` | 11 | — |
| `ProbeText` | 10 | 2 |
| `EdgeScroll` | 10 | 2 |

`DebugSidebar.rei` is two lines and seals 47 values, which is the general shape
here: leaf modules expose one `view` and everything else was incidental.

`WorkerMessagingSection.rei` is just `include DebugSection.S;` — that moves its
contract check from the `(module ...)` pack site in `DebugSidebar.re:751` to the
definition itself.

confirmation that all 267 values are used internally. `src/` remains at the
detector's fixpoint. Unlike the util PR — where `Tree.equal_struct` fell out —

- **`CustomStatics.custom_statics_deferred_ap` discards `~ancestors`**, and its one

  tried annotating the parameter `list(Id.t)` to match its two siblings and it does
  not compile. Harmless while the parameter is discarded; a trap if anyone ever
  reads it. Deciding what it *should* receive is a semantic call, so the `.rei`
  records the situation instead.
- **`Abbreviate.AbbrevBudget.split_evenly` is exported only because
  `Test_Abbreviate` covers it directly** — no `src/` caller. Noted in the interface

and `Abbreviate.AbbrevBudget.with_budget` from outside now fails with

title: Add .rei interfaces for 12 src/util modules
body:
Without an interface, every top-level binding in a module is exported, so the
compiler can never tell you one is unused. Adding a `.rei` turns warning 32 back
on — and it is a hard error under `--profile release`, which
`deploy_branches.yml:69` gates on. So for these 12 modules, unused code now fails
CI instead of accumulating.

Each interface declares only the module's real external surface, so anything used
solely inside its own file becomes private. `JsUtil` alone hides 12 helpers
(`date_now`, `find_scroll_container`, `QueryParams.get_arguments`, …).

264 lines of interface, 23 of them restated types.

## Which 12

Picked by how many lines of type declaration you would have to maintain in two
places — not by file size:

`ListUtil` 64 · `JsUtil` 60 · `StringUtil` 27 · `Unicode` 25 · `Tree` 23 ·
`OptUtil` 19 · `Aba` 18 · `VarMap` 9 · `StructureShareSexp` 8 · `Direction` 5 ·
`Either` 4 · `FloatingElement` 2

## What's excluded

- **`Menu` (70 restated type lines) and `OpenRouter` (101).** Inline
  `module M: { … } = { … }` sealing gets the same coverage with the signature
  written once. `Id.re:142` already does it that way.
- **`include <third-party>` modules** — `BigInt`, `Sets`, `Maps`, `MapUtil`,
  `IntMap`, `Result`. `BigInt` is 14 source lines and extracts to 184; `refmt`
  cannot parse it. Such an interface is a hand-copy of someone else's API that
  breaks on their next release.
- **`Util.re`**, which dune treats as the library interface module.

## It found two dead functions immediately

`Tree.equal_struct`, and then `Tree.equal` once that went. **The index-based
detector could not see either** — both match its `^equal` ppx-name suppression,
which exists because ppx-generated call sites do not appear in the index at all.
Worth knowing that the two tools miss different things.

## Tooling

`scripts/gen_rei.sh` / `make rei FILE=...` generates a starter interface:
`ocamlc -i` over the ppx-expanded source dune already built, piped through
`refmt`. Output is refmt-clean so `@src/fmt` accepts it. It strips the library's
own alias prefix, since `-short-paths` renders siblings as `Util.Either.t`, which
is a dependency cycle inside `src/util`.

One gotcha if you write one by hand: **a `.rei` can declare fewer derivers than
the `.re` and still compile**, because the ppx wraps generated values in
`[@@@ocaml.warning "-32"]`. That drift only surfaces as `Unbound value` at a
consumer. Structural drift is caught immediately.

## Verification

`make test-quick`: 3,225 passing. dev, test and release builds clean — release is
the one that matters, since dev will not fail on the unused values a new interface
exposes.

title: Delete dead stylesheets, CSS rules, and unreferenced image assets
body:
26 files, **−1,640 lines**. **No compiler can check any of this**, so the liveness
argument matters more than the diff. Three commits, each using a progressively
stronger test.

## 1. Three whole stylesheets

- **`assistant.css` (833 lines)** — every rule is scoped under `#assistant`, and
  nothing renders `id="assistant"`. The sidebar's HelpfulAssistant panel renders
  `AgentView.view` (`Sidebar.re:340`), styled by `style/agent/*.css`, which is
  where every class the agent UI actually uses (`send-button`,
  `message-container`, `message-identifier`, `llm-identifier`, `dot1`, …) is
  defined. The only unscoped rules — `.llm-selector`/`.llm-label`/`.llm-dropdown`
  — are unreferenced in source.
- **`project.css` (315 lines)** — styles a projects/file-system UI that no longer
  exists. All five ids and 18 of 20 classes have zero source references; the other
  two are generic (`.cell`, `.icon`) matched only as descendants of the dead ids.
- **`agent.css`** — empty file, imported nowhere.

## 2. Individual rules, judged by source grep

22 rule blocks across 9 stylesheets, 12 unreferenced icons, and
`style/palette.html` (a design swatch page nothing links to and no dune rule
copies into the build).

The test is deliberately over-cautious. A selector counts as **live** if any of:

- its name appears as a string literal anywhere in `src/` or `test/`;
- **some literal is a prefix of it**, since classes get concatenated —
  `"depth-" ++ string_of_int n`, `"agent-md-h" ++ string_of_int level`,
  `"highlight-code-" ++ c`, `"slash-card-" ++ kind`;
- **its name appears as a bare OCaml token.** `Sort` and `cls` constructors reach
  the DOM through `show`/`to_string` and never appear as a literal at all — that
  is `.Mod`, `.Sig`, `.MPat`, `.Rul`, `.EmptyHole`, `.Single`. A naive
  literals-only scan called all of those dead.

That took the candidate list from 72 names to 22, each then re-checked by hand for
both hyphenated and underscored spellings.

A rule is removed only when **every** comma-separated selector is dead, judged by
the key (rightmost) compound: `.projector.probe .window-toggle` can only match an
element carrying `.window-toggle`, so it goes even though `.projector` is live.
Rules whose key compound is an element selector are left alone
(`.step-back:hover span` survives) — which leaves a few orphans but cannot break
anything.

## 3. The stronger test: grep the compiled bundle

If a class name appears nowhere in the 11 MB `hazel.js`, no code path can put it
on an element, so any rule naming it is unreachable. Controls confirm the test
discriminates rather than trivially passing: `projector` 108 hits, `probe` 256,
`hsod` 9, `depth-` 4, `highlight-code-` 1, `agent-md-h` 3.

Ten classes still defined in CSS can never be emitted, and their rules go:
`developer-notes-display`, `view-icon-button`, `deselected`, `call-cursor`,
`click-kbd-pill`, `is-index`, `qr-when-unfocused`, `window-toggle`, `step-back`,
`step-expand`. Nine are ones commit 2 deliberately spared for having an element
key selector — unreachable all the same, since nothing carries `.step-back`.

**`call-cursor` is a correction.** Commit 2 kept it because `call_cursor` exists in
source — but that is a function name; the hyphenated class is never emitted. The
source-grep test was wrong there and the bundle test is right. That is the honest
summary of why there are two commits instead of one.

Where a rule mixed dead and live selectors, only the dead branches are dropped:
`.prompt-display, .developer-notes-display` keeps `.prompt-display`. One such trim
initially took the rule's leading comment with it, because the dead branch was
listed first and carried the preceding trivia — restored.

## Browser verification

Done, and it covers all three commits: probe sidebar (including
`#sample-focus-bar` with a focused sample, and probe hover cards with kbd badges),
agent panel, agent main menu, nut menu, editor context menu, stepper (took a
step), tutorial mode (completed a step, checkmark renders), exercises mode with
grading reports, and the projectors slide. No console errors, no unstyled surfaces.

If you re-verify: **restart the browser rather than hard-reloading** — a stale Web
Worker survives a reload and reports `EXN:TypeError reading '1'` from eval, which
looks like a real regression and is not.

`licenses/Icons.md` is a blanket Noun Project attribution rather than per-icon, so
removing unused icons does not affect it.

title: Add telemetry sections to the Debug sidebar (Evaluation, Statics, Editor & Memory, Frame Timing)
body:
Adds four Debug sidebar sections — **Evaluation**, **Statics**, **Editor &
Memory**, **Frame Timing** — showing where a keystroke's time goes and what the
editor currently holds. They share a table, a formatter and a heat map with
#2370's **Worker Messaging** panel, which moves onto the same pieces.

## Up front: refs and side effects, deliberately

The collectors are module-level refs, written by side-effecting calls at the
points being measured rather than values threaded through the component tree.
Deliberately: this is developer instrumentation — tangential to the codebase, off
a normal user's path, inert unless a panel is open — and doing it properly would
mean widening every `update` / `calculate` signature along the way to carry a
value only a debug panel reads. Worth revisiting if these panels ever become
load-bearing.

What a section touches is still closed: each collector and `PerfFormat` has a
`.rei`, each section is pinned to `DebugSection.S`, and the mutation stays inside
the collectors.

## What gets collected

**Stage timings, per keystroke.** The edit action's `perform` (update phase), then
each calculate-phase stage — statics + elaboration, the syntax-cache rebuild
(MakeTerm + Measured), cursor info, the ExplainThis color map — and the total. 30
frames kept; a stage that didn't run shows `—`, never a misleading `0`.

**The eval round trip, per request.** The latency the main thread sees
(`postMessage` → `onmessage`) beside the worker's own evaluator time, which it now
returns in a new `eval_time` on `ServerMessage.result` — so the gap between them
is queue + serialization + transfer. Plus the outcome, encoded payload sizes and a
restart count. 10 requests kept.

**Structural counts, per frame.** Info-map entries, error and warning counts, why
statics ran or didn't (recomputed / forced / deferred / cached), segment tokens,
tiles, rows, projectors, and live undo/redo/backpack depth.

Durations are `Core.Time_ns.Span`, sizes `Core.Byte_units`. Byte-exact heap sizes
are deliberately absent — walking the heap per frame is too expensive, and timings
plus counts answer the question.

## The changes, in reading order

1. **`util/Metrics.re`** (new) — the gate and bounded history every collector
   shares, as a functor; recorders run through `when_enabled`. Read first.
2. **`util/PerfMetrics.re`** — per-frame collector: the `frame` record, the
   `time_*` stage wrappers, the count recorders.
3. **`util/EvalMetrics.re`** — round-trip collector, keyed by request id so its
   rows line up with Worker Messaging's.
4. **`util/WorkerMetrics.re`** — pre-existing; moved onto the functor.
5. **`CodeEditable`, `CodeWithStatics`, `Page`, `History`** — where the timings
   are taken, and where gating syncs once per cycle.
6. **`util/WorkerServer.re`, `util/WorkerClient.re`** — evaluator time on the
   wire, and the recording around the request lifecycle.
7. **`sidebar/PerfFormat.re`** — the table vocabulary: a `column` carries header,
   tooltip and cell projection; `cell` is opaque; `view` assembles a body.
8. **`sidebar/*Section.re`** — one per panel: columns plus a `view` call.
9. **`sidebar/SidebarModel.re`, `Settings.re`** — sidebar settings store
   `debug_expanded`, so the whole Debug sidebar starts collapsed.
10. **`util/TimeUtil.re`** — `timed`, and the `span` alias that lets a deriving
    type carry a `Time_ns.Span`. The only file outside `src/web/`.

## Closed panels cost nothing

Each collector is gated on **its own** section being expanded, synced once per
cycle in `Page.Update.calculate`, and every section ships collapsed — so ordinary
editing pays nothing.

## Testing

`make dev` clean, `make test-quick` green (3311), and a manual pass over all five
sections in Chrome. `Test_WorkerServer` covers a `Time_ns.Span` surviving Marshal
+ `structuredClone` and its nanosecond json encoding.

title: Report a mismatch once: tuple components and function bodies; describe tuple shape mismatches
body:
Fixes #1958. Fixes #2507.

A term whose child already reports a mismatch against its expected type is no longer reported again itself, for tuple components and for function bodies. Tuple shape mismatches (arity, labels) say what differs.

**Before.**
- `let (a : Int, b : Int) = (1, "s") in a` produced three errors: `Expecting type Int but got inconsistent type String` on `"s"`, and `Expecting type Int, Int but got inconsistent type Int, String` on both the tuple and the parentheses around it. Arity and label mismatches were reported the same way, by printing both full types.
- `let f : Int -> Bool = fun x -> x + 1 in f(1)` produced two errors: `Expecting type Bool but got inconsistent type Int` on `x + 1`, and `Expecting type Int -> Bool but got inconsistent type Int -> Int` on the whole `fun`, whose synthesized type was built from the already-marked body. With the function shorthand (`let f(x) = x + 1` as a module member checked against a signature) the second error sat on the synthetic `fun` the desugaring introduces, which has no source span.

**Now.**
- **Tuples.** A component that already reports a mismatch contributes its expected type to the tuple's synthesized type, so the tuple, and the parentheses that forward its marks, do not repeat it. A labeled element `l=e` does the same for its value. The first example is one error, on `"s"`.
- **Functions.** A body that already reports a mismatch contributes the expected return type to the function's type, so the function is not marked again. The second example is one error, on `x + 1`. A non-function against an arrow type is still reported on itself.
- **Tuple shape.** A mismatch of the tuple's own shape is still reported on the tuple and now says what differs: `Expecting a tuple of 2 elements but got 3 elements`, or `Expecting a tuple of 2 elements with labels name, age but got 1 element with labels name; missing label age`, in the CLI and the cursor inspector alike. `LabeledTupleStaticsHelpers.shape_mismatch` computes the summary once for both. A same-shape mismatch on a non-literal (a variable of tuple type) keeps the generic message, where the two types are the useful information.

Both rules are the one line `List.exists(Mark.is_expectation_mismatch, child.marks) ? expected : child.elab_syn_ty` at the parent's type construction, in the `Tuple`/`TupLabel` and `Fun` cases of `Statics.re`.

**Tests.** The annotated-tree test for `(_=1) : (_=String)` pins the mark on the value only; tests for single reporting of a component and of a body (let-bound and as a function argument), for arity, and for a non-function against an arrow type; unit tests for `shape_mismatch`.

## Verification

`make dev` clean · `make test-quick` green (3476 tests).

title: Modules II, part 9: the standard library as modules (proof of concept)
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Proof of concept, like #2508, and not close to done.** It exists to show
> what the standard library looks like once modules are real values, and to
> find out what that costs. Read "Known gaps" before reviewing anything else.

Ninth of the stack, on top of #2508. The standard library becomes modules,
and ships the vocabulary the implicits feature needs.

```
List.map([1, 2, 3], fun x -> x * 2)          -- [2, 4, 6]
String.of_int(42) ++ String.uppercase("ok")  -- "42OK"
Float.sqrt(9.0) >. Float.pi                  -- false
Option.map((Some(2), fun x -> x + 1))        -- Some(3)

let implicit A = ShowInt in
let show = fun (implicit S : SHOW, x : S.T) -> S.show(x) in
show(3)                                      -- "3"
```

## What it does

- **Six modules**: `List` (all 65 list functions), `String`, `Int`, `Float`,
  `Option`, `Pair`. The list family is the one that crowds the namespace
  worst: `map`, `filter`, `length`, `find` and `head` are all top-level
  names today.
- **Every flat name stays.** `String.length` and `string_length` are the
  same function, so no program, slide or exercise changes meaning. The
  modules are the front door from here on; nothing is deprecated in this PR.
- **Both halves are derived from the same records.** A module builtin is an
  ordinary constant whose type is a signature and whose value is a module,
  and the signature's member types and the module's member values come from
  the same builtin, so a member cannot drift from the function it names. A
  member is the implementation, not a copy: it is the term the flat name is
  bound to.
- **`SHOW` and `ORD` ship as signature types**, with an instance per base
  type: `ShowInt`, `ShowFloat`, `ShowBool`, `ShowString`, `OrdInt`,
  `OrdFloat`, `OrdString`. Each carries a manifest type member, since
  resolution selects on it.

## Two decisions worth arguing with

**The instances are not ambient.** A program marks what it wants, one line
per instance. Making them ambient is a language decision rather than a
library one, and it needs a priority or coherence rule first: with none, a
program that defines its own instance for a base type under any other name
makes every call ambiguous against the shipped one. Twelve of the implicits
tests change meaning when they are ambient, which is the same warning from
the other side. The cost is a `let implicit A = ShowInt in` line, which is
what the Module Implicits slide already writes.

**No `EQ`.** Polymorphic `==` already compares two values of a type, so an
equality signature earns its keep only once a type can choose its own
equality, which wants the sharing constraint #2495 lacks.

## Two prerequisites this found, fixed where they belong

Both are in #2493, with tests, because plain source hits them:

- A module member's name is its label, but substitution renamed it away from
  capture like any binder, so `M.x` stopped finding it. The stepper
  substitutes the whole builtin environment, so any module with a member
  named after a builtin lost that member.
- A capitalized module name parses as a constructor, and a known constructor
  won, so a module whose name matched one could not be projected at all. The
  JSON type contributes `List`, `Int`, `String`, `Float` and `Bool` to every
  program's constructor namespace, which made exactly the five most useful
  stdlib names unusable: `module List = { let f = 1 } in List.f` was an
  error. Projecting a constructor means nothing, so the module now wins in
  dot position, and `List([Int(2)])` still builds JSON.

The one change here is in the evaluator: a member holding a fixpoint has to
unroll, so a projection judges a definition the way a variable lookup does,
sharing one predicate. Only a module that came out of the environment can
hit it, which is why it is in this PR rather than #2493.

## Known gaps

1. **Cost per mention.** A module out of the environment is copied on each
   mention, so `List.map` copies a 65-member module where `map` copies one
   fixpoint. I have not measured it against a hot loop, and if it matters the
   answer is probably to bind the library once per program rather than to
   hand it out of the environment, which needs a prelude mechanism that does
   not exist.
2. **The grouping is partial.** The tuple-label operations, the ADT helpers,
   the `Ord` inversion, `print`, the SInt and Nat families and the remaining
   conversions are still only flat. `Bool` has nothing worth grouping yet.
3. **`Int`, `Float` and `String` cannot be *declared* as modules in the text
   grammar**, since those are base-type tokens: `module Int = {…}` does not
   parse, though the shipped ones are fine because nothing declares them in
   source. The editor accepts it.
4. **Nothing is deprecated.** Two names for every function is the price of
   not breaking programs, and there is no mechanism to mark the flat ones
   legacy.
5. **No `List` for other collections.** There is no `Set`, `Map` or `Seq`
   because there are no such builtins; this PR groups what exists.
6. **`Option`'s type member is `Option`'s sum type**, so `Option.T` names it,
   but the module cannot expose the constructors: constructors declared in a
   module are not members of it (#2243).

## Verification

`make dev` clean · `make ci-check` clean under the release profile ·
`make test-quick` 3845 green · new suites `Statics.BuiltinsModules` (11) and
`Evaluator.BuiltinsModules` (10), including that a member equals its flat
function and that a recursive member unrolls through a projection · CLI
probes for every module and for both signatures.

Expect the same two per-seed `Full tests` failures as the rest of the stack,
both unrelated and both dev's: the cyclic-alias crash in normalization and
the `:+` printer divergence explained on #2493.

title: Charts as a Hazel library over the HTML substrate
body:
Charts, without bundling a charting library into Hazel.

Replaces the d3-backed chart projector in #2350 (which this supersedes — that
approach put the whole chart vocabulary inside the implementation, so every new
chart kind, scale, or annotation was an OCaml change *plus* a JS change, and
`ChartProj` could not be tested at all because its output only existed inside
d3's DOM).

Here there is no `Chart` type and no chart projector. A chart is an ordinary
`HTML` value built from this branch's `Node` and `Create` escape hatches (which
render SVG), and the charting vocabulary — scales, nice-domain rounding, tick
selection, axes, bands, arcs, legends, palette — is Hazel source in
`hazel-programs/charts/charts.hz` that a reader can fork. Adding a stacked bar
or a log scale is a change to Hazel code. No d3, no npm additions.

### What the implementation gains instead

Not chart knowledge — a way to draw *values*:

- **`HtmlRenderer`**, a rich probe (`^^probe_html`), renders a probe sample as
  whatever its value describes: static HTML as DOM, or an
  `(init, update, view, subs)` 4-tuple as a running app keyed on the probe's id.
  This is what a computed chart needs — `Chart.bar(sales)` is an application, so
  its HTML only exists after evaluation. It is the value-side counterpart to
  `HTMLProj`, and mirrors its two commit modes.

  When the probed expression is *itself* html, a handler commits by **rewriting
  the source** to `f(H)` and letting the program's own pipeline evaluate it —
  splicing the handler by the name the evaluator recorded on it, so the edit
  lands on the definition and every call sees it. Evaluating the transform inside
  the renderer cannot work: a probe has no elaborated syntax and no environment
  to resolve `f` in.

- ~~**`View.docked`** lets a projector send a secondary surface to the Projectors
  panel while keeping its inline presence — distinct from

title: Modules II, part 6: expectations reach sub-modules and destructured binders
body:
Sixth of the stack, on top of #2500. The signature's expectations now reach into sub-modules and destructuring patterns, so a problem is reported where it is.

- **Sub-modules.** `module Inner = …` items receive the sub-signature the outer signature declares for them.
