title: SPIKE: compile the Hazel evaluator with wasm_of_ocaml and benchmark it
body:
## What this is

A **spike**, not a merge candidate. It answers one question: is Hazel's
evaluator meaningfully faster compiled by `wasm_of_ocaml` than by
`js_of_ocaml`? The evaluator is compute-bound and already runs off the UI
thread in a Web Worker, which makes it the part of Hazel most likely to
benefit from Wasm GC — boundary-crossing costs, which is where Wasm usually
loses, barely apply there.

## The constraint that shaped the whole branch

`virtual_dom` v0.16 requires `js_of_ocaml < 6.0.0`. `wasm_of_ocaml` is only
released from 6.0.1 onward. **They cannot coexist in one opam switch.**

Everything else here follows from that:

- the benchmark links only `language` + `menhirParser`, never `haz3lcore`
  or `web`;
- parsing goes through `menhirParser` rather than the zipper path the CLI
  uses, since `PersistentZipper`/`MakeTerm` live in `haz3lcore`;
- `language` had to be made Bonsai-free, which is what the `util` split and
  the livelit removal are for.

## Changes

- **Split `util`** into `util` (pure + `js_of_ocaml` only) and `util_web`
  (Bonsai/Virtual_dom). `Util_web` re-exports all of `Util`, so most
  consumers only changed `open Util` to `open Util_web`. `JsUtil` and `Key`
  were each *split* rather than moved, keeping their `js_of_ocaml`-only
  majority in `util` — that alone avoided ~48 files of churn.
- **Dropped livelits from the language core.** The three builtin livelits
  construct vdom directly and were the last thing holding `Virtual_dom`.
  `LivelitCtx` keeps its types so `Ctx.LivelitEntry` still typechecks, but
  nothing populates it and `LivelitProj` renders a placeholder.
- **Added `bench/wasm/`**: the benchmark, a switch-setup script, and a
  runner that builds both backends from the same compiler version.
- Bumped `(lang dune 3.16)` to `3.17` for `(modes wasm)`.

Resulting dependency closure is
`language → util → {ptmap, bignum, uuidm, unionFind, csv}` — verifiably
Bonsai-free.

## What it gives up

The livelit deletion is the part that must not merge. The principled version
registers livelit views from the web layer rather than deleting them; the
`util` split, by contrast, is worth keeping on its own merits and is the
same prerequisite an Internet Computer port would need.

Two livelit tests were removed (`^slider(50)` elaboration, `^emotion(50)`
statics-map ids) because they assert behaviour the builtins provided. The
`^^slider` tests exercise the projector, a separate mechanism, and are
untouched.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `dune build @check` (dev) | clean |
| `dune build src` (release, `-warn-error +A`) | clean |
| `@test-quick` | 3457 tests, 0 failures |
| benchmark runs end-to-end on node 22 | yes |

## Numbers

Not yet — the comparison needs the second opam switch, which is still being
built. A `js_of_ocaml` 5.9.1 smoke run gives 607 ms plain / 596 ms incr on
`bench/eval-bench.hz`, but that is *not* the baseline: `run.sh` rebuilds
both backends from the same 6.x compiler so the delta is attributable to the
backend rather than the toolchain. Results to follow in a comment.

Caveat worth stating up front: `eval-bench.hz` is a single workload. Under
`wasm_of_ocaml` the OCaml heap is managed by the browser's collector rather
than OCaml's, so allocation-heavy and allocation-light programs may not move
in the same direction — one number is a signal, not a characterization.

## Running it

```
bench/wasm/setup-switch.sh
git worktree add --detach ../hazel-wasm-bench wasm-eval-bench-spike
cd ../hazel-wasm-bench && bench/wasm/run.sh hazel-wasm 20
```

Node 22+ is required; Wasm GC postdates the node 18 this repo otherwise
builds against.

title: Report each error once, not once per wrapper
body:
Follows #2488, and parked here rather than folded into it until reviewers weigh in on which layer the fix belongs in (see https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/pull/2488#issuecomment-5529767668).

## The problem

A transparent wrapper restates the marks of the term it wraps — `Parens` and `Projector` in `Statics` pass `~marks` straight through — so one error occupies a chain of nested ids and the problems sidebar lists every one of them:

| program | static errors reported |
| --- | --- |
| `y` | 1 |
| `(y)` | 2 |
| `((y))` | 3 |
| `^s(1)` (mistyped `expand`) | 1 |
| `^^livelit(^s(1))` (same) | 2 |

Not livelit-specific, but guaranteed to bite for livelits: a use is always inside a projector, so a `BadLivelitExpansion` was always duplicated.

## The fix

Collapse each chain at the collection layer (`ProblemCollection.make_problem_context`). `Statics` hands a wrapper the child's mark list itself, so physical equality identifies exactly the ids that inherited a mark — never two equal-looking marks on unrelated terms — and the innermost id of a chain is the one that owns it.

Ids under a projector have no measurement of their own, so when the owner of a mark is hidden the row is reported at the innermost wrapper the user can actually see: the projector. That keeps the row clickable and lets it highlight with the caret.

`statics.error_ids` is untouched, so code decorations — including the projector's own error styling — are unchanged.

## The open question

The alternative is to stop propagating marks through wrappers in `Statics` at all. Cleaner in principle, but the projector's error decoration reads the projector node's info, so it would go with it. Happy to move the fix there instead if that's the preference.

## Testing

Four cases added to `Test_ProblemCollection`: parens don't multiply an error, a collapsed chain reports the marked term, a projected livelit use reports one error, a hidden marked term reports at its projector. `ProblemCollection` (19), `UserLivelits` (34), `AgentTools` (174) and `ErrorPrint` (5) pass.

title: Add Hazel build info to top bar of editor
body:
Displays the git information for the current Hazel build as an unobtrusive, always-visible indicator in the top-right of the top bar, plus in the page title, so it's clear which build you're looking at when juggling multiple branches/tabs. Originally written by @7h3kk1d and developed by @CyrusD123; design revised per review discussion (the earlier git-icon slide-out panel was heavier than this information warrants).

## What it shows

`branch@short-sha[-ahead][-dirty] · #PR`, in a color only slightly darker than the top-bar background — legible if you look for it, invisible if you don't.

- **branch** links to the branch on GitHub; **short-sha** links to the commit (links always present; an unpushed commit's link starts working after push).
- **`-ahead`** marks commits not yet pushed to the upstream branch; **`-dirty`** marks uncommitted local changes (addressing the request to distinguish these).
- **`· #NNNN`** appears when the branch has an open PR, linked to it. Detected at build time via the `gh` CLI (`scripts/build-info.sh`) — an *optional* dependency: if `gh` is missing, unauthenticated, offline, or there's no open PR, the segment is simply omitted. Since the `BuildInfo.ml` rule re-runs on every rebuild and the `gh` call costs ~0.4s, the lookup is cached per branch in `.git/hazel-pr-cache` (steady-state rebuilds pay ~0.06s, same as the git-only rule); a `pre-push` hook deletes the cache since the answer most often changes around pushes. The hook activates once the `core.hooksPath` installation from #2233 lands; until then (or without `gh`), staleness is bounded by branch switches, and deleting the cache file forces a re-query.
- The **page title** becomes `hazel · branch@sha[-suffix]`, except on a clean, pushed `dev` build where it stays plain `hazel`.

## Selectability

The label is drag-selectable for copying to a collaborator — you can start the selection anywhere in the top bar's empty space and sweep across. This took some spelunking: mousedown over non-focusable page regions moves focus to `#page`, whose `on_blur` handler re-focuses the clipboard shim mid-gesture, destroying the nascent selection (the sidebar avoids this only because it has a `tabindex`). Fixes: `tabindex="-1"` on the indicator so it swallows focus like the sidebar; exemptions in the `#page` copy/cut handlers so Cmd+C copies the selected label rather than the editor selection (and Cmd+X doesn't delete editor content); sidebar-style `user-select` descendant rules; non-draggable anchors; and the label kept as a single inline span (selection across flex items is unreliable). The same tabindex + exemption treatment could make other UI text selectable in future PRs.

## Removed

The bottom-bar git-icon slide-out panel, its `build_info_expanded` setting, the git icon asset, and the associated CSS.

## Test plan
- [x] Indicator renders with branch/sha links; `-ahead`/`-dirty` suffixes appear and disappear as commits are made/pushed (observed live during development)
- [x] Open-PR detection: `BuildInfo.ml` generated with `Some 2315` + URL on this branch; `None` fallback verified with `gh` off PATH
- [x] PR cache lifecycle: first build writes `.git/hazel-pr-cache`; cache hit serves the PR with no network (verified with `gh` off PATH); `pre-push` hook invalidates; post-invalidation build without `gh` degrades to `None`
- [x] Drag-selection from empty bar space, glyphs (both directions), padding, and bar edge — verified via automated CDP tests in headless Chrome
- [x] Copy event over a build-info selection passes through natively (clipboard shim untouched); editor copy/cut behavior unchanged elsewhere
- [x] Page title: `hazel · branch@sha-suffix` on this branch; plain `hazel` on clean dev
- [ ] Reviewer: sanity-check on a machine without `gh` installed

title: Deduplicate three copy-pasted implementations
body:
Eight files, +145/−308. Three independent de-duplications, one per commit. Unlike
the rest of the stack these *change* code rather than delete it, so each commit
carries an argument for why the surviving version is equivalent.

## 1. Grading primitives and the SVG icon helper

`Grading.re` documents itself as the shared primitives module and
`CodeGrading.re` does `include Grading;`. **`TutorialGrading.re` did not** — it
re-declared `type percentage`/`points`/`score`, `score_of_percent`, `score_view`
and `percentage_view` verbatim, down to the `Printf` format strings. Replaced with
`include Grading;`, which also picks up `pending_score_view`, the one primitive it
had not copied.

Separately, `icon_size`/`simple_icon` were byte-identical in `Icons.re` (web) and
`TableRenderer.re` (haz3lcore). `haz3lcore` cannot depend on `web`, so it had been
retyped. Hoisted into `Util.SvgUtil`, which both libraries reach and which already
opens `Virtual_dom`.

## 2. Point `Tutorial.re` at `EditorUtil.append_exp`

`append_exp` existed three times. `EditorUtil.re` is canonical; `CodeExercise`'s
copy was already dead and went in the preceding branch; `Tutorial`'s was the last
live duplicate.

**Verified equivalent rather than assumed**, because the two built annotations
differently:

| | Tutorial | EditorUtil |
|---|---|---|
| base case | `IdTag.fresh()` | `IdTag.mk([Haz3lcore.Id.mk()], empty_secondary)` |
| recursive | `IdTag.mk_internal(ids(e1))` | `IdTag.mk(ids(e1), empty_secondary)` |

`IdTagged.re:36-47` makes `mk_internal(ids)` structurally equal to
`mk(ids, empty_secondary)`, and `fresh()` equal to
`{ids: [Id.mk()], secondary: empty_secondary}`.

The remaining question was whether `Haz3lcore.Id.mk` and the `Id.mk` resolved
inside `IdTagged.re` are the same generator — **there are three modules named `Id`
in this repo.** Both `src/language/Id.re` and `src/haz3lcore/Id.re` are
`include Util.Id;`, so they share the one `Uuidm.v4_gen` closure.

Constructor coverage is also identical: both dispatch recursively on exactly
`Seq`, `Filter`, `Let`, `Theorem`, `TyAlias` and `Use`, and both put the same 41
constructors in the catch-all — including `ModuleExp`, which an earlier copy
handled recursively.

## 3. Functorize `SliderProj` / `SliderFProj`

63 lines each, 52 identical — the entire difference was `Bigint` vs `float`: which
atom they read, which atom they build, how they render. `SliderCore.Make` now holds
the shared body and each variant supplies only that difference, 14-16 lines apiece.

`Atom.t` is the natural seam: both were matching `Exp({term: Atom(Int(i)), _})` /
`Atom(Float(f))` and rebuilding the same way, so `PARAMS` asks for
`of_atom`/`to_atom`/`to_string` and nothing else.

Net −17 lines, which undersells it — the point is that a change to slider
behaviour is now one edit rather than two that can drift apart.

Failure message wording is preserved (`"Slider: Get: not integer literal"`,
`"SliderF: Put: not float literal"`) via a separate `literal` label rather than
being degraded to the module name. `ProjectorInit.re:12-13` references
`SliderProj.M`/`SliderFProj.M` and is unchanged.

## Verification

`make test-quick`: 3,225 passing. dev, test and release builds clean.

Both sliders were also exercised by hand in the browser — dragged each, and the
cursor inspector read `Projector (Slider) : Int` and `Projector (SliderF) : Float`.
That check matters here because a functor that typechecks can still be wired to the
wrong literal, and no test covers projector interaction.

title: De-web the language and core libraries
body:
## Summary

The `language` and `core` (`haz3lcore`) libraries no longer depend on js_of_ocaml /
Vdom and now compile as ordinary native OCaml. All web-specific code (Vdom views, DOM
listeners, the LLM agent layer) moves out into the `web` library.

This is the base for a stacked PR — **#2354** adds a native terminal UI on top of it.
(Previously this branch also contained the TUI; that has been split out into #2354.)

## De-webbing

- **`util`**: web-only modules (`BonsaiUtil`, `*MenuListener`, `FloatingElement`,
  `JsUtil`, `SafeTriangle`, `SvgUtil`, `WebUtil`) move into the `web` library. Regex,
  grapheme segmentation, and URI coding get pure implementations (`Unicode`,
  `StringUtil`, `API`); `Key.re` is dropped.
- **`language`**: livelit *views* move to a web registry; `Livelit.re` keeps only the
  core definitions.
- **`core`**: each projector is split into pure core logic (stays in `core`) and a web
  Vdom view (`web/projectors/`). Time and DOM-focus become **injection points**
  (`CoreEffects` in `web`). The LLM agent layer moves to `web/agent/`. The `Keyboard`
  keymap moves into `core` so it no longer lives in the web library.
- **Projectors**: pure helpers lift to file level (`docs/projector-backend-split.md`);
  `TableProj` gains a sizing-backend hook (`WebApprox` vs `TextGrid`) so a non-web
  frontend can reserve exact space — the web keeps `WebApprox`.
- **`nativecheck`**: a native smoke-check executable parses and evaluates `1 + 2` with
  no js_of_ocaml dependency, guarding against native-buildability regressions.

## Tests

- Harness split so web-free suites run natively (`haz3ltest.exe`, ~2750 quick tests, no
  node) and the seven web-dependent suites run under node (`haz3ltest_web.bc.js`).
  Shared modules live in `haz3ltest_common`; see `haz3ltest.re` / `haz3ltest_web.re`,
  `run_node.sh`, `run_tests`, and `test/dune`.

title: Stale grout after remold: prepending use-in to -5 gives 'in <grout> -5'; caret there crashes the view (Not_found)
body: Type `-5`, move the caret to the start, type `use Float in `. Result: `use Float in ⬡-5`, with a convex grout between `in` and `-5`. Clicking on the `-5` region — or moving the caret into it (e.g. cmd-right) — kills the page with "Exception during View: Not_found". Found by @Negabinary during review of #2419; reproduces on dev (6b611ba3be). The final segment is `Grout(Convex)` directly followed by `-` molded *prefix* (convex left nib) — a malformed operand-operand junction. How it gets there: at the intermediate state `use Float i¦ -5` the `-` molds infix and regrouting inserts a convex grout as its left operand; when `in` completes the use form, `-` remolds back to prefix, but the grout survives — `Relatives.regrout`'s right-trim branch keeps a grout when `Grout.fits_shape(g, s_l)` holds, which only consults the left neighbor's shape (`in`'s concave nib), never the grout's right neighbor (now convex). The crash is downstream: MakeTerm absorbs the `-` and `5` tiles into a hole without registering their ids in the terms map, and `Arms.term_range` does an unchecked `Id.Map.find(Piece.id(p), syntax.terms)` (Arms.re:370), so the view raises Not_found whenever the caret indicates either tile. It needs `-`'s infix/prefix duality plus `use`'s intermediate states: `use Float in ` before `!true` is clean, and `let`/`if`/`fun` wrappers before `-5` are clean. Test-harness repro: `mk({|¦-5|}) @ string_to_ltr_actions("use Float in ")` ends with two segment tiles missing from `CachedSyntax.terms`. Two fix loci: regrout should drop trim grout that doesn't fit both neighbors, and separately Arms.re could use `find_opt` so a piece missing from the terms map degrades gracefully instead of killing the view.

title: Fix: retain probes when fast-parsing almost-complete syntax
body:
the menhir fast parse path supports complete and almost-complete terms... specifically it supports things that would be terms if a hole was inserted at the end. however, fast-parsing such almost-complete things currently loses probes.

eg say a `.hz`  file ends in a semicolon:

```
let f = fun x -> x + 1 in
^^probe(f(1));
^^probe(f(2));
```

this loads with both probes attached but reprints without them, so `./hazel format` and any save of a loaded-but-unedited buffer destroy the probes.

Cause: menhir rejects the dangling `;`, FastParse's append-a-hole retry strips the hole it added, and loading was the one path into the editor that doesn't regrout,  so the buffer ends in an operand-less `;`, `Segment.skel` fails on it, and `Triggers.refractor_seg_to_seg` gives up and reprints the program without its `^^probe(...)` wrappers (invocations nested inside tile children survive, which is why body-less let chains usually looked fine).

Fix: `PersistentZipper.parse_text` regrouts after unzip, same as every edit. Saving such a fragment spells the materialized hole (`...f(2));¿`) and is a fixed point thereafter.

closes #2450

title: CI: in-place opam-repository edits can retroactively break our lock file
body:
## What happened

On 2026-06-03 every CI run on every branch started failing at `opam install . --deps-only --with-test --locked`:

```
[ERROR] Package conflict!
  * No agreement on the version of conf-pkg-config:
    - deps-of-hazel → conf-libssl >= 4 → conf-pkg-config >= 5
    - deps-of-hazel → conf-pkg-config = 4
```

ocaml/opam-repository#29976 edited already-published package versions in place: `conf-libssl.4`, `conf-libffi.2.0.0`, and `conf-zlib.1` now require `conf-pkg-config >= 5`, conflicting with our locked `conf-pkg-config = 4`. Fixed by #2333, but nothing prevents a recurrence — opam package metadata is mutable, and upstream routinely edits existing versions (especially of virtual `conf-*` packages) rather than cutting new ones.

## Why this hurts

- It breaks **all** branches simultaneously, not just dependency-update PRs — unrelated work gets red CI overnight with no code change on our side.
- The breakage is external and time-triggered, so bisecting our history finds nothing.

## Proposal: pin the opam repository to a commit SHA in CI

`ocaml/setup-ocaml@v3` accepts an `opam-repositories:` input, so workflows could use `https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository#<sha>`. The daily `update_deps` workflow would bump the SHA alongside the regenerated lock file, so upstream changes only ever land (and fail) in the `bot-update-deps` PR, never on existing branches.

Note on why we'd want both the SHA pin *and* the lock file: an opam lock file pins which versions the solver picks, but not their metadata — the repository can edit a published version's dependencies after the fact (no content hashes, unlike npm/cargo lock files). The repo SHA freezes the metadata; the lock file freezes the version selection and keeps installs reproducible for local development against the default repo. Each covers a hole the other leaves open.

Maintenance cost: the pin lives in several workflow files unless factored out (e.g. into a single env/var or composite action), and the `opam-repository-archive` repo we also add would ideally be pinned the same way.

Refs: #2333, ocaml/opam-repository#29976

title: ci: fix Actions cache eviction, split into independent jobs, enforce release warnings on test/
body:
Part of the CI/CD plan on #2203. Closes #2456.

## What changed

- **Replaced the one serial job with three independent ones.** `Build and Deploy Hazel` was a
  single 21–31.5 min job that published the preview and *then* ran the tests — one check covering
  everything, with the test result buried after a deploy that had already happened. Now
  `Fast checks`, `Full tests` and `Deploy branch preview` are three jobs with no `needs:` between
  them. Each re-runs alone, so a flaky suite costs one job rather than another deploy and another
  30 minutes, and the fast signal comes back in ~4 minutes instead of at the end of the full run.

- **Turned off `setup-ocaml`'s dune cache and made the opam switch cache single-writer.** Its
  entries are keyed on the run id, so they never hit, and 10.24 GiB of them were evicting the
  `_opam` switch from a 10 GiB budget. The switch cache is now `restore` + `save` with
  `dev`/`bot-update-deps` as the only writers, plus `restore-keys` for a warm start after a
  lockfile bump.

  Caching the switch ourselves is deliberate and unsupported: `setup-ocaml` declines to do it
  (ocaml/setup-ocaml#1098), on the grounds that cached dependencies drift from opam-repository.
  We take that trade knowingly — it moves `Install dependencies` from 3–7.5 min to ~6 s, which is
  what sets how long we wait for a deploy and for static-check feedback — and the lock file bounds
  the risk. It doesn't eliminate it: in-place edits to already-published packages have broken us
  before (#2334).
- **Added `make ci-check` to enforce release warnings on `test/`** (#2456). `dune build @check
  --profile release` type-checks both trees without linking — 21 s, no second build of the test
  bundle. Warnings in `test/` previously printed and passed.
- **Made test failures produce a non-zero exit code.** Alcotest is run with `and_exit:false` so
  the JUnit report can be written first, and junit_alcotest hands the outcome back as a function
  to call afterwards — the only thing that propagates a failure. `test/haz3ltest.re` discarded
  it, so the test binary exited 0 whatever happened, and every entry point keyed on that exit
  code passed on a red suite: `dune runtest`, `make ci`, `make test`, `make test-quick` and
  `./run_tests`.
- **Published the test reports as check runs** (`use-actions-summary: false`). The default writes
  results to the run's job summary and creates no check run, so `Test Report` never appeared in a
  PR's check list — nothing to click through to, no inline annotations on failing tests, and
  nothing that could be named as a required status on `dev`.

## What runs where

```
checks.yml   ── on: workflow_call                       the definitions, one copy
   ├── Fast checks       fmt → make ci-check → make ci-quick → Quick Test Report
   └── Full tests        make ci → Test Report → Codecov

ci.yml       ── on: push, except gh-readonly-queue/** | merge_group
   └── calls checks.yml

fork-ci.yml  ── on: pull_request, if the pull request comes from a fork
   └── calls checks.yml, with the report and coverage steps off

deploy.yml   ── on: push, except gh-readonly-queue/**
   └── Deploy branch preview    release build → hazel.org/build/<branch>
```

Every filter is a trigger rather than an `if:`, which leaves **two conditionals in the whole
system**: the fork test, and one input that turns off the report check runs and the Codecov
upload for forks, whose `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only and which get no secrets.

**`ci.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger on purpose.** A same-repo pull request fires both it and
`push` for the same commit, so the full suite would run twice. Forks are the only case `push`
cannot see — a fork's pushes happen in the fork — and `fork-ci.yml` covers them.

**Fork PRs gain CI.** Today's `deploy_branches.yml` is `on: [push]`, so fork PRs get no checks at
all; 3 of the last 200 PRs here came from forks. They now get `Fast checks` and `Full tests`,
without the report check runs their token can't create. They still get no branch preview.

**No merge queue exists yet**, but both `ci.yml` triggers are load-bearing once one does. A queue
pushes its `gh-readonly-queue/**` branch, yet Actions only reports status into the queue from a
`merge_group` run — so the trigger is what makes the queue's checks exist, and `branches-ignore`
is what stops the same commit being checked twice and a speculative merge being published as a
preview. Turning the queue on is #2203 phase 4.

**Why formatting, warnings and the quick suite share a job.** Every job installs OCaml and the
dependencies independently, ~2 min warm and 5–9 min cold, which is more than those three checks
cost to run. Splitting them would buy precise names and precise retry for roughly double the
wall clock. Worth revisiting after the build-once artifact work in the follow-ups, which is what
makes extra jobs cheap.

`Build release` is no longer a separate gate — the deploy job runs the same command. That leaves
`src/web`'s `main` and `worker` jsoo executables unlinked on fork PRs and in the merge queue,
which we're accepting until it causes a problem; `Full tests` still links the `web` library
through the test bundle.

## Notes for merge

- **`make test` and `./run_tests` now fail on a red suite.** That's the point, but it may surface
  failures that have been passing silently across the open PRs — #2128's evaluator/stepper QCheck
  flake most likely.
- The strict formatting gate wasn't in the original plan and can turn other branches red. Easy to
  drop.
- **The warm-cache win can't be demonstrated until this reaches `dev`.** Only `dev` and
  `bot-update-deps` write the switch cache, so the first push after merging populates
  `Linux-opam-*` and the *second* is where `Install dependencies` should fall to single digits.
- **Branch protection and the merge queue are both future work** (#2203 phase 4). When you set
  them up, the required checks are named `CI / checks / Fast checks` and `CI / checks / Full
  tests` — the reusable-workflow nesting makes those non-obvious, so it's noted in `ci.yml` too.
  The `merge_group` path is the one thing here that can't be exercised until a queue exists.
- ~~Also pins the opam repository, resolving #2334.~~ Reverted in bd8c01b3b2 — a separate concern
  that made this harder to review. #2334 stays open and gets its own PR.

title: CI: release-profile warnings aren't enforced on test/, so warning cruft accumulates there
body:
## Problem

The `release` profile promotes OCaml warnings to errors, and that's the pass that gates PRs. But CI only ever compiles `test/` under the **dev** profile, which is deliberately lax. So warnings in `test/` print into the job log and the job still goes green.

### Concrete example

[Run 32063723487 / job 95490665795](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/actions/runs/32063723487/job/95490665795?pr=2435) (PR #2435) concluded **success**. Its `Run Tests` step printed, twice:

```
Warning 33 [unused-open]: unused open Dune__exe.EditingPrelude.
```

(`test/Test_ReparseDocSlides.re:10`.) Compile the exact same tree under `release` and it's a hard error:

```console
$ dune build test/haz3ltest.bc.js --profile release
File "test/Test_ReparseDocSlides.re", line 10, characters 0-19:
10 | open EditingPrelude;
     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Error (warning 33 [unused-open]): unused open Dune__exe.EditingPrelude.
$ echo $?
1
```

## Why it happens

`.github/workflows/deploy_branches.yml` has two build steps, and neither compiles `test/` strictly:

| Step | Command | Profile | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Build Release` | `dune build @src/fmt --auto-promote src --profile release` | release | **`src` only** |
| `Run Tests` | `make ci` → `dune runtest --instrument-with bisect_ppx --force` | **dev** (no `--profile`, so the default) | `src` + `test` |

`test/` is the only source tree in the repo with a `dune` file that never sees `--profile release`.

To be clear, the dev/release split is working as designed and is worth keeping — dev's laxness is what makes local iteration fast (`src/util/dune` states it outright: dev `-warn-error -A`, release `-warn-error +A-58`; elsewhere dune's own per-profile defaults do the same job). The bug is only that the strict pass is *scoped* to `src`.

## Current debt

Exactly **one** error today, on a clean `test/` rebuild under release (dune keeps going past the first error by default — `--stop-on-first-error` is opt-in): the `Test_ReparseDocSlides.re:10` unused open above. That's small enough to fix in the same PR that adds the gate, which is the argument for doing it now rather than after it grows.

## Possible fixes

1. **Extend the release build to cover `test`** — `dune build @src/fmt --auto-promote src test --profile release`. One-line change, gates everything. Cost: `test/` gets compiled twice per run (once under release for the gate, once under dev + `bisect_ppx` for coverage).
2. **A dedicated strict step/target** — e.g. a `make ci-strict` running `dune build test --profile release`, kept separate from the instrumented coverage run.
3. **Not** making dev strict for `test/` — that would defeat the purpose of the dev profile locally.

No dune changes are needed either way: `test/dune` has no `(env)` stanza, so it already inherits dune's strict release defaults. Only CI's scoping has to change.

## Related

- **#2422** (`ci-cache-and-job-split`) is already reorganising these jobs into separate deploy/test steps and drops `--auto-promote` from the CI entry points — probably the natural place to land this.
- Same root cause, adjacent gap: the release step checks `@src/fmt` but not `@test/fmt`, *and* passes `--auto-promote`, so formatting violations in either tree get silently rewritten in a throwaway checkout instead of reported.

title: Parameterized types and multi-binder polymorphism
body:
This PR introduces first-order parameterized type constructors, a tuple-arrow kind system, type-level type functions, and a clean separation between value-level and type-level type abstraction. It also threads multi-binder polymorphism through the existing `poly`/value-level type-application machinery.

## User-facing changes

### Parameterized types
Hazel now supports parameterized type aliases:

```hazel
type Option(a) = + None + Some(a) in
type Either(a, b) = + L(a) + R(b) in
type List(a) = + Nil + Cons(a, List(a)) in
let xs : List(Int) = Cons(1, Nil) in xs
```

- A declaration with `n` parameters introduces a type constructor of *tuple-arrow* kind `(Type, …, Type) -> Type`. Applying a constructor to its `n` type arguments at once produces an ordinary type.
- Tuple-arrow kinds are atomic: `Either(Int, Bool)` is well-kinded, but `Either(Int)` is rejected as `expects 2 arguments, got 1`. Extra parens disambiguate single-tuple-arg vs multi-arg: `Either((Int, Bool))` is also a 1-of-2 arity error, while `List((Int, Bool))` is a list of pairs.
- Recursive aliases stay implicit, including non-uniform recursion: `type List(a) = + Nil + Cons(a, List((Int, a)))` works and runs to completion.
- Constructors are introduced with polymorphic schemas: `Some : poly a -> a -> Option(a)`, `L : poly a, b -> a -> Either(a, b)`, etc. Implicit instantiation works in analytic positions (`Some(3) : Option(Int)`), and the same constructor can be used at multiple specializations in one program.
- Modules can export parameterized aliases: `module M = { type L(a) = + Nil + Cons(a, L(a)) }` and `M.L(Int)` resolves correctly through the module's exports.

### Type-level type functions: `typfun`

Aliases can be written with the prefix-binder syntax:

```hazel
type Option = typfun a -> + None + Some(a) in
type Either = typfun a, b -> + L(a) + R(b) in
```

This is the same alias as `type Option(a) = …` / `type Either(a, b) = …` (same kind, same constructor schemas).

A *curried* form is also supported and stays curried:

```hazel
type PResult = typfun err -> typfun ok -> + Error(err) + Ok(ok) in
type StringResult = PResult(String) in     // kind Type -> Type
type R = PResult(String)(Bool) in          // fully applied; kind Type
```

`PResult` has kind `Type -> Type -> Type` and accepts curried application. Partial applications are well-kinded and may themselves be used as alias bodies.

### Value-level type abstraction: `abs` (renamed from `typfun`)

To free the `typfun` keyword for the type-level form above, the value-level type abstraction (System F's big-Lambda) is now spelled `abs`:

```hazel
let id : poly a -> a -> a = abs a -> fun x : a -> x in
let pair : poly a, b -> a -> b -> (a, b) =
  abs a, b -> fun x : a -> fun y : b -> (x, y) in
pair@<Int, Bool>(3)(true)
```

Multi-binder `poly`, `abs`, and the value-level type application `e@<T1, T2>` are now first-class: a single `Poly(TPat.Tuple([a, b]), …)` binds both at once, and `e@<T1, T2>` reduces in one step. Curried explicit nesting (`poly a -> poly b -> …` / `abs a -> abs b -> …`) keeps its curried structure.

A new `Mark.TypAbsApplyArityMismatch` is emitted at the `@<…>` node when the type-arg count doesn't match the function's `Poly` arity (e.g. `e@<Int>` for a 2-binder `Poly`); the result type is `Unknown` so downstream value-arg type-checking doesn't see a body with leaked free type variables.

### Prelude updates

- `Option(a)` and `Either(a, b)` are now parameterized aliases (kinds `(Type) -> Type` and `(Type, Type) -> Type`).
- `Either`'s constructors are renamed `Left`/`Right` → `L`/`R`.
- The `_opt`-family list functions and `partition_map` use `Option(?)` and `Either(?, ?)` in their signatures so the cursor inspector shows the parameterized form rather than the expanded `+ None + Some(?)` sum.
- `string_compare` returns `Ord` (the named alias) instead of the expanded sum.

### Cursor inspector & error messages

- Type aliases now display as declarations: `type Either(a, b) = + L(a) + R(b)` rather than `Either :: typfun a, b -> + L(a) + R(b)`.
- A type-pattern's class label distinguishes "Type alias" from "Type parameter" based on its statics classification.
- New focused marks: `TypKindMismatch`, `TypParamApplyNonArrowKind`, `TypParamApplyArityMismatch` (callee + arity), `TypAbsApplyArityMismatch`, `TPatParamNotAtAliasHead` (e.g. `poly T(a) -> …` is rejected with a clear message).
- Kind errors stay localized to the offending node (no longer spread to surrounding `+` / `,` tokens).
- Free type variables in `TypParamAp` callees produce a single mark (the free-variable mark on the var), not a redundant "cannot apply" mark too.
- Constructor highlighting / jump-to-definition is type-directed: when two sum types in scope each declare `B`, `B(true) : OneOfThree(_, _, _)` resolves to `OneOfThree`'s `B`, not the innermost shadowing one. Constructors declared inside a module also highlight correctly.
- Hovering on `M.PList` lights up `PList`'s declaration site inside `M`.

### Identifier syntax
Capitalized identifiers (constructors, module names) accept trailing primes — `Result'`, `M''`, etc.

### ExplainThis
- Dedicated forms for parameterized types, multi-binder `poly` / `typfun` / `abs`, multi-arg type application, and module / signature decls, with arity-dispatched explanations for arity-1/2/3 forms.
- Per-form highlighting for module/signature item decls.
- `Module Definitions` items get correct dropdowns and highlighting.

### Other surface changes
- Sum types render as `+Lt + Eq + Gt` (space after the leading `+`, spaces on both sides of interior `+`s) instead of the previous `+ Lt + Eq+ Gt`.
- Constructor arguments in sum types render without doubled parens: `Cons(a, List(a))` instead of `Cons((a, List(a)))`.

## Internal changes

### AST additions

`src/language/term/Grammar.re`:

- `Typ.TypFun(tpat, typ)` — type-level type function.
- `Typ.TypParamAp(typ, typ)` — type parameter application.
- `Typ.TypTuple(list(typ))` — multi-arg bundle (only ever the second arg of a `TypParamAp`; no kind on its own).
- `TPat.Param(tpat, list(tpat))` — alias-head form `T(a, b, …)`.
- `TPat.Tuple(list(tpat))` — multi-binder list, used as the binder of `Poly` / `TypAbs` / `TypFun` / `Rec` for comma-separated forms.
- `TPat.Parens(tpat)` — transparent parens wrapper so user parens get their own tile id.
- `Exp.TypAbs` — renamed from `Exp.TypFun` (the value-level type abstraction).

### New module: `Language.TypKind`

```ocaml
type t =
  | Unknown
  | Type
  | Arrow(list(t), t);
```

`apply_all` consumes a tuple-arrow kind's argument list in one step (atomic; no partial application of multi-binder kinds), but a curried `Arrow([Type], Arrow([Type], Type))` accepts arguments one per `TypParamAp`. `Unknown` is consistent with everything and absorbs application. `to_string` renders single-arg arrows as `k -> r` and multi-arg as `(k1, …, kN) -> r`.

### Single source of truth for kinds

`Statics.kind_of_typ` is now a top-level helper. `TyAlias` calls it once on the alias body and threads the result through `Ctx.extend_alias(~typ_kind=…)` (so downstream `Var(name)` references see the right kind via `lookup_tvar_typ_kind`) and `utpat_to_info_map(~alias_kind=…)` (so the cursor-inspector message at the alias name agrees).

### `TypExpectation.AnyKindExpected`

A new variant on `TypExpectation.t` distinguishes alias-body positions (any kind is fine — the alias inherits the body's kind) from value-annotation positions (must be kind `Type`). This lets the strict kind-`Type` check live where it belongs without firing on legitimate higher-kinded constructs (a curried alias body, a partial parameterized application used as an alias body, a `TypFun` alias body, …).

### Higher-kinded recursive types

`type List(a) = + Nil + Cons(a, List(a))` is stored as `Rec(List, TypFun(a, Sum[Nil, Cons(a, TypParamAp(Var("List"), a))]))` — a fixed point at kind `* → *`. `weak_head_normalize` intentionally treats `TypParamAp(Rec(_, TypFun(_, _)), _)` as a normal form so recursive types don't infinitely expand. `Typ.unfold_one` performs one step of μ-unrolling for callers (constructor matching, sum extraction, structural meet across `Sum`/`Rec` shapes) that need to peer inside. `Typ.apply_args` peels one `TypFun` per `TypTuple` element for multi-arg applications.

### Multi-binder substitution and reduction

- `Typ.subst_many` and `DHExp.ty_subst_many` substitute a list of types for a corresponding list of binders in one step.
- `Transition.TypAp` zips a `TypTuple` argument against a `TPat.Tuple` binder element-wise. Single-binder forms substitute as before.
- Polymorphic constructor schemas are a single `Poly(TPat.Tuple([a, b, …]), ty)`, never a curried chain.
- `Equality` and `Typ.meet` flatten multi-binder `Poly`s element-wise via `TPat.binders_of`. A binder list of all holes is treated as a wildcard so the `Poly(EmptyHole, _)` placeholder used as `TypAp`'s callee analysis target matches any `Poly` regardless of binder shape.

### Module exports

`ExpandModule.collect_type_exports` now handles `Param` tpats: it builds a single `TypFun(TPat.Tuple([a, b, …]), body)` over the params (wrapped in `Rec` for self-referential definitions) and `Ctx.extend_alias`-es it with the matching `(Type, …) -> Type` kind. The exported field's tile is annotated with the original alias declaration's id so var-highlight on `M.T` recovers the binding site.

### Parsing

- The new keywords (`abs`, `typfun`, `poly`, `typlam`, `forall`, `rec`) are listed in `Token.keywords` so `should_add_space` keeps the space between keyword and a leading `(`.
- `MakeTerm.binder_of_tpat` lifts a comma-separated tpat `MultiHole` into a `TPat.Tuple` (preserving an outer `Parens` wrapper if present).
- `MakeTerm.apply_typ_param_args` normalizes `T(a, b, …)` into `TypParamAp(T, TypTuple([a, b, …]))` while leaving `T((a, b))` as `TypParamAp(T, Prod([a, b]))`. The sum-variant extractor reverses this locally so `Cons(a, b)` in a sum-type position remains a constructor with a `Prod` payload.
- The Menhir parser, AST, and conversion layer all gain matching nodes (`TypParamAp`, `TypTuple`, `TypFunType`, `ParamTPat`, `TupleTPat`).
- `Precedence.dot = 10` (was 22) so `M.T(Int)` parses as `(M.T)(Int)`. Slide files were migrated via `scripts/migrate_dot_precedence.sh`.

### Substitution bug fix
`Substitution.in_exp` previously substituted into the RHS of `Let` / `Theorem` using the *extended* env, which would alpha-rename free occurrences of the bound name in the RHS itself. The non-recursive RHS now uses the outer env. A regression test `Test_Stepper` covers the case (`{ let y = 1; let y = y }` and similar).

### Property-based testing

The QCheck random term generator now exercises modules, parameterized type aliases (`type T(a, …) = body` and the typfun-bodied form), `TypFun`, `TypParamAp`, multi-binder `poly` / `abs`, `e@<T1, T2>`, and `T.x` projections — round-trip and statics-preservation properties cover all the new forms.

### Test coverage

- `test/statics/Test_Statics_ParameterizedTypes.re` (new) — kind errors, arity mismatches, multi-arg application, constructor elaboration, curried `typfun`, partial application as alias body, etc.
- `test/statics/Test_Statics_Modules.re` — parameterized type aliases inside modules.
- `test/evaluator/Test_Evaluator_TypAp.re` — runtime reduction, including non-uniform recursion and multi-binder TypAp.
- `test/Test_Typ.re` — β-normalization, recursive family lookup.
- `test/Test_VarHighlight.re` — type-directed constructor lookup, module-internal constructors.
- `test/Test_Menhir.re` and `test/Test_MakeTerm.re` — both syntaxes for parameterized types, the renamed `abs` keyword, `T(a, b)` argument normalization, multi-binder forms.

### Documentation

- `docs/parameterized-types.md` — the parameterized-types story (this doc deliberately doesn't cover `abs` / value-level type application; that's described in this PR).
- `docs/modules.md` — interaction with parameterized types.

## Test plan
- [ ] `./run_tests test '' -q` passes (currently 2704 tests, all green)
- [ ] Manual smoke: `type Either(a, b)`, `type Option`, `Some(3) : Option(Int)`, `L("a") : Either(String, Int)`
- [ ] Manual smoke: `abs a, b -> fun x:a -> fun y:b -> (x, y)` and `f@<Int, Bool>(…)`
- [ ] Manual smoke: `type T = typfun a -> typfun b -> body`, `T(String)(Bool)`, `T(String)` as alias body
- [ ] Manual smoke: `module M = { type L(a) = + Nil + Cons(a, L(a)) }`, `M.L(Int)`, jump-to-definition on `M.L`
- [ ] Cursor inspector: kinds shown correctly on alias names, parameter names, `T(args)` callees

title: Fix cross-term id collisions in ExpToSegment pad_ids
body:
In a pretty-printed program with two multi-case `case` expressions, the k-th rule tile of each case ends up with the SAME id: several `pad_ids` call sites pass the `List.tl` of a term's ids without `~base`, so for freshly-parsed single-id terms the base falls back to `Id.invalid`, and the deterministic `Id.derive("pad<k>", invalid)` sequence repeats across terms. Anything grouping shards by tile id then misbehaves — observed as a `Highlight.of_tile: shard mismatch` crash (three 2-shard rule tiles under one id). Same latent collision for list-lit commas, deferred-ap commas, module semicolons, pat list-lits, and derivation rules.

Fix: pass `~base` = the term's head id at all seven sites, as pad_ids' own doc comment prescribes.

title: PBT all of it
body:
# Full-syntax PBT generators

Our PBTs ran against hand-written generators covering a curated subset of the
language — no modules, no `theorem`/`forall`, no invalid tiles, labeled tuples only
in a few positions. This replaces them with ppx-derived generators that reach **every**
constructor of the Menhir AST, and fixes everything that fell out.

One commit adds the generators, one commit per suite flips it over and fixes what it
finds, one commit deletes the old generators. Each migration commit is self-contained.

Two things that change across the board:

- **`size` changed meaning.** `arb_exp(50)` was a node budget; `arb_exp_full(5)` is
  depth fuel, halved per recursive step. Counts drop 10 000 → 1 000: full-syntax terms
  are far more expensive to build and evaluate. Wider per term, fewer terms.
- **Failures are real.** The generator only emits terms the printer and Menhir lexer
  round-trip, and `Canonicalize` absorbs genuine print aliases, so a failure means a gap.

---

### `Stop ExplicitNonlabel shrinkers from looping forever`

- `shrink_{exp,pat,typ}` returned `ExplicitNonlabel` *for* `ExplicitNonlabel` — a
  shrinker yielding its own input, so QCheck never terminates. Now `Iter.empty`.

### `Add ppx-derived full-syntax QCheck generators`

Derives `arb_exp_full` / `arb_typ_full` from the Menhir AST. Shaping needed to stay
inside what the lexer and printer can express:

- Identifiers, livelit names (`^name`), constructor names get `[@gen]` so they stay
  lexically valid.
- `Invalid*` payloads draw from a closed face-token set (`^o^`, `?_?`, …) — the junk
  tiles MakeTerm actually classifies as `Invalid`. Operator-shaped junk (`!!!`) molds
  as an infix with holes instead, so it's useless as an `Invalid` example.
- Lists capped at 0–3; the ppx default reaches ~10k and explodes recursive terms.
- `TupLabel` left sides restricted to `Label` / `ExplicitNonlabel` — the only forms
  that print and parse as `lab=e` / `_=e`.
- `UnknownType` only generates the printable `EmptyHole`; `Module` binders are
  `VarPat` only; `DynamicErrorHole`'s payload must parse as an error sexp.

Also:

- `ppx_minimal_idents` lets a suite ask for `x`/`y` instead of random letters, so
  generated programs actually bind things.
- Generators are memoized by fuel — building one eagerly expands to
  ~`positions^log2(n)` closures, and rebuilding per suite OOMs Node.
- `Conversion.Typ.of_core_type_provenance` raised on any provenance but
  `Internal`/`EmptyHole`, which crashed shrinking (it goes through `~rev`). Every
  provenance now maps to a printable form.
- Sort-specific renames: `ExplicitNonlabel` → `ExplicitNonlabel{,Pat,Type}`.

### `Migrate Test_Grammar PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- One-liner. Annotation map/unmap was already total.

### `Migrate Test_Elaboration PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- `case (()) | _ => [(let `a` = x in x)] end` — a quoted-label binder synthesizes
  `Label("a")`, which reached `Coverage.all_ctrs_of_type` and hit its
  "non-normalized type" `failwith`. A `Label` isn't a sum; it joins the non-sum forms.
- Bare `_` in pat sort is `ExplicitNonlabel` at the MakeTerm tip, but `PatternMatch`
  only knows `Wild`. Elaboration now emits `Wild` and keeps the mark.

### `Migrate Test_Statics_Properties PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

This suite asserts elaboration is a fixed point, so every fix is about idempotence.

- `x((?))` where `x` is an unknown builtin — dynamics raises `InvalidBuiltin` for
  anything outside `Builtins.forms_init`. Unknown names now elaborate to `Invalid`
  (Indet under `Transition`, same synthesized type). Not `Var`, which would resolve
  against an enclosing binding of the same name.
- `proof_of` quoted the *user* term while `elab_term` held the elaborated one, so
  re-elaboration produced a type that wasn't `fast_equal` to the recorded one — and
  broke the side condition on the `(ProofObject, ProofOf)` ascription rule. Both now
  quote `e_elab`.
- `FixF` wrapped its body in `Asc` unconditionally, adding a layer per pass. Now only
  when the ascription would change the body's type.
- Constructor patterns recomputed `elab_ty` even when already resolved, regressing it
  to `Some(None)` on the second pass.
- Test side: the elaborated program must be re-checked with `use_mode = None`.
  `use SInt in -?` elaborates to an `SInt` minus, which a `Some(Int)` pass rewrites
  back to `Int`. (`CachedStatics` already does this.)

### `Migrate Test_Evaluator_Properties PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

- `let y = y in y` → substitution produced `let y' = y' in y'`. The RHS isn't under
  the binder, so freshening a shadowing binder must not rewrite it.
- `fun x -> 1` with a `Sig` in the annotation slot — only *surface* ascriptions go
  through `desugar_sig`, so substitution met a `SigLet` pattern inside a type and hit
  a `failwith`. Signature names are field labels, not expression binders, so we
  recurse and leave them alone; statics also normalizes `Fun`'s annotation now.
- `fix x -> (theorem ? = y in x)` — `Theorem`/`Forall` step to Indet but their bodies
  still mention environment variables. Without `wrap_closure`, big-step left `x` free
  while small-step substituted.
- `forall x(x) -> x` — big-step alpha-renames the later binder, small-step doesn't.
  `Alphas.combine` is first-match, so duplicate binders need the *later* binders
  passed first to shadow correctly.
- `DynamicErrorHole((()))` — the `req_final` binder shadowed the outer term, so
  `wrap_closure` wrapped the child and dropped the hole.

### `Migrate Test_TextRoundtrip PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- One-liner. The print→parse→print fixed point already held.

### `Migrate Test_Menhir PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

The big one — Menhir↔MakeTerm equivalence is what full syntax exposes most.

**Menhir learns the syntax it was missing:** `theorem`, `forall`, `proof_object`,
`proof_of`, `Nat`/`SInt`, quoted labels in pat and typ position, invalid faces in every
sort, `module _ =` / `module ? =`, `hint <exp> test … end` (was string-literal only),
and `undef` → `undefined`.

Two restructurings:

- **`sumTerm` derives `typ`.** MakeTerm classifies *any* type in sum position —
  `TypVar` → `Variant`, else `BadEntry` — so `sumTerm` does too. Because it can then
  derive a leading-plus sum, `+ A + B` reduced to `Sum([BadEntry(Sum …)])` where
  MakeTerm has a flat sum; `splice_sumterm` flattens it back.
  Heads of *no-lead* sums (`Nil + Cons(Int, T)`, `HasInt(Int) + HasMore(...)`) get
  their own nonterminal, since an applied constructor isn't a `typ` and a general
  `sumTerm PLUS …` head would be swallowed by the leading-plus rules.
- **`typ` split into `typ`/`typ_inner`** so `...` sits looser than `->`, matching
  `Precedence`. `%prec` can't express it — `TUPLE_EXTENSION` also carries exp-level
  precedence. Function params gain a layer so ascription binds tighter than cons:
  `fun p : T :: q ->` is `ConsPat(AscPat(p,T), q)`, as MakeTerm reads it.

**Where the two parsers disagreed:**

- `undefined . ((`l`))` — Menhir erases parens, so the `.` field tip has to peel them
  or MakeTerm sees a field access and Menhir a `MultiHole`. Same for `=` tips.
- `{ o^o }` — MakeTerm collapsed a leaf `Invalid` in mod position to a hole, which
  erases the token entirely.
- `^w^ -> Int` — an invalid face is an *Exp*-sorted tile, so it drags the whole type
  out of Typ sort and the arrow vanishes. `(^w^) -> Int` agrees. Precedence can't fix
  this: an invalid hole is atomic, so it never trips the paren check.
- `?:+^w^` — same trap, but a sum has no single protectable operand; the ascription
  itself is lost. So a sum containing an invalid gets parenthesized whole.
- `hint _ test _ end` with a nested `test … end` — during LTR insert, `test` matched
  deep in the backpack and completed `HintedTest`'s own shard instead of expanding a
  nested `Test`. Leading expanders now only match at the top of the stack (as
  ambiguous polymorphs already did), and hints are force-parenthesized.
- `|=>` inside `{}` — `remold` skipped complete kids when parent sorts matched,
  leaving a stale mold whose empty `in_` then broke MakeTerm.
- `(A ... B) ... C`, `T . A -> B` — the parsers order `.`, `->` and `...` differently;
  the printer now parenthesizes defensively on both sides.
- `Invalid(s)` was rewritten to the fixed string `"Invalid"` on the way back to the
  Menhir AST. That runs during shrinking, so shrinking silently turned counterexamples
  into *different programs* — and `"Invalid"` lexes as a constructor, not a face.
- Bare `lab=e` only parses inside `(…)`, so it wraps at binders and at the root while
  tuple fields don't become `((a=1), (b=2))`.
- Module bodies were an unimplemented TODO in the parenthesizer; item payloads are now
  parenthesized and item expressions wrapped so a printed `;` stays a separator.

**`test/Canonicalize.re`** is the new normalizer: it rewrites a generated term into the
shape print+parse produces (`BuiltinFun` → `Var`, `Nat`/`SInt` → `Int`, floats via
their printed form, `DynamicErrorHole` stripped, bare `TupLabel` → singleton tuple,
`f(_)` → `DeferredAp`). Round-trip and cross-parser tests canonicalize both sides and
then compare *strictly*, instead of loosening the equality relation — one place to look
when a print alias shows up, and `Equality` stays honest.

### `Migrate Test_MenhirFuzz PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- Same switch, and it drops its own bespoke equality settings for `Canonicalize`.

### `Migrate Test_ExplainThis PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- No production fix needed — `decide` handled everything. Adds a regression test
  walking every info-map entry of `let 0 = _ in []` and `fun 0 -> []`.

### `Remove the curated AST generators`

- Deletes ~580 lines of hand-written generators and their wrappers.

---

Side effect worth noting: menhir's arbitrarily resolved reduce/reduce conflicts drop
from **52 on `dev` to 5**, and it no longer reports any never-reduced productions
(`dev` has 3). Shift/reduce goes 57 → 69.

Delete dead code, to a fixpoint
body:
176 files, **−5,589 lines**, +16. **Worth reading commit-by-commit rather than as
a single diff** — the commits are deliberately ordered so each is independently
checkable, and squashing them together makes the reasoning impossible to follow.

| area | files | removed |
|---|--:|--:|
| `src/web` | 52 | −1,678 |
| `src/language` | 38 | −1,213 |
| `src/haz3lcore` | 35 | −1,058 |
| `src/pretty` | 14 | −880 |
| `src/util` | 20 | −607 |
| `test` | 13 | −119 |
| `src/CLI`, `src/menhirParser`, dune/opam | 4 | −34 |

## Kept at reviewer request

Review round 1 did exactly what the PR asked for — people recognised things they
wanted. **19 definitions across 12 files are restored** in "Restore definitions
reviewers asked to keep". They are listed here rather than tracked by the
detector, so this table is the record: `make dead-code` reports every one of them
again, by design.

| restored | file | asked by | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `err_msg` | `language/term/InvalidOperationError.re` | @Negabinary | "wanna use it shortly" |
| `fresh` | `language/term/MPat.re` | @Negabinary | `MPat` was the only term module missing one |
| `temp` ×3 | `language/term/{Sig,Mod,MPat}.re` | @Negabinary | same — three had lost it, not one |
| `print_timestamp` | `util/JsUtil.re` | @Negabinary | "don't want to look up how to do this again" |
| `print_time_prefix`, `print_time`, `print_times`, `measure_time` | `util/TimeUtil.re` | @Negabinary | "looks useful" |
| `Debug` | `haz3lcore/projectors/implementations/ProbeProj.re` | @disconcision | "would prefer to keep this" |
| `empty`, `listlit_lbl`, `mod_lbl` | `haz3lcore/lang/Token.re` | @disconcision | used in #2389 |
| `sorted_children` | `haz3lcore/tiles/Tile.re` | @disconcision | used in #2374 |
| `abbreviate_pat` | `language/term/Abbreviate.re` | @disconcision | used in #2115 |
| `shard_index` | `haz3lcore/zipper/action/Indicated.re` | @disconcision | used in #1959 |
| `to_actions` | `web/app/Log.re` | @Negabinary | wanted by the log-replay work |
| `exercise` ×3 | `web/exercises/examples/Blank*Exercise.ml` | @Negabinary | **these are templates** — see below |

The `Blank*Exercise.ml` files are the one place the sweep was simply wrong. They
were hollowed out rather than deleted, leaving a nine-line header that ends
*"…and edit the arguments below"* with nothing below it. They are unreferenced
**by design**, in the same way as the entry-point files the detector already
exempts — a template nobody has instantiated yet has no callers and never will.

## If you wanted something here, say so

The detector finds definitions with **no recorded reference**. It cannot tell rot
from:

- an API deliberately built out ahead of its callers,
- an escape hatch kept around for debugging,
- work someone has in progress on another branch and hasn't wired up yet.

All three look identical to "dead". Round 1 caught the items above; if there is
more, a comment on the relevant commit is enough, and everything here is
recoverable from git history.

## The commits

1. **Delete the dead `src/pretty` library.** 866 lines, 14 modules, zero
   references anywhere — no `Pretty.*` use, no `open Pretty`. The apparent hits
   are `PrettySegment`, an unrelated module in `haz3lcore`. It stayed compiled
   only because `src/web/dune` listed it in `(libraries)`. Removing it also drops
   **the 12 `Obj.magic` calls in `MeasuredLayout`/`Box`/`LayoutOfDoc` — the only
   ones in the repo outside js_of_ocaml DOM interop** — and
   `src/pretty/{ListUtil,Unicode}.re`, which duplicated `src/util` verbatim
   because the library declared no `(libraries)` and so could not see it.

2. **Empty files, orphan modules, commented-out code.** Two 1-byte files;
   `ReadTools.re` (115 lines, never wired into `CompositionUtils.re`'s tool list
   while its six siblings have 3-18 references each); `LogEntry`, `FailedInput`,
   `ExerciseUtil`; and 57 consecutive commented-out lines in `CodeGrading.re`.

3. **111 unused top-level definitions.** Largest: `RuleImage.of_sort` (133
   lines), `API.node_request_streaming` (81), `Indentation.go'` (46). Densest:
   `Icons.re` (11 unused SVG icons, including `add_file`/`add_folder`/
   `add_project` from the removed projects UI).

4. **Dead code exposed by the previous sweep**, to a fixpoint: 8 more in round
   two, 1 in round three, 0 in round four. Notably `Sidebar.switch_assistant`,
   whose only caller was the old assistant tab handler.

5. **Dead definitions found by the index**, to a fixpoint: 3,769 lines across 134
   files. This is the category the text scan structurally could not see — 58
   members nested inside `module X = {...}` blocks, and functions whose only
   callers are their own recursive calls (`Segment.remold_sig_uni`,
   `CodeExercise.append_exp`, `ValueChecker.check_value_mod_ctx`).

6. **Dead types, constructors and write-only record fields** — the category the
   index cannot see *at all*, because `[@deriving]` emits ghost occurrences for
   every constructor at the type declaration. Found by hand, each checked
   individually. Includes `SafeTriangle.active_state`'s
   `exit_point`/`menu_direction`, which are written in `activate` and never read;
   warning 69 cannot see this because they *are* written.

7. **`OptUtil.filter`**, restored — it became live on `dev` while this branch was
   open.

8. **Restore definitions reviewers asked to keep** — the 19 above, plus four
   dangling comments left behind by earlier deletions (`Typ.re`, `API.re`,
   `TutorialGrading.re`, and an over-long rationale in
   `Test_Evaluator_Properties.re`).

## What was deliberately not deleted

The part I would most like scrutinised, because it is where judgement replaced
mechanism.

- **Anything a ppx can synthesise a call to** without it appearing in source:
  `Sample.{show,sexp_of,…}_targets`, `RichProbe.show_packed_*`,
  `RichProbeRegistry.yojson_of_packed_action`, `ConstructorMap.equal_constructor`,
  `Tree.equal_struct`. `Sample.re`'s are reached from `EvalInfo.re`'s
  `[@deriving sexp]` on a `Sample.targets` field.
- **Comment blocks that carry knowledge rather than rot**: the `pp` overrides in
  `Annotated.re`/`IdTagged.re` are documented debugging affordances;
  `ProofRule.re`'s disabled `BinOp` rule carries a TODO about negation and
  implication plus a type-level sketch of an in-progress feature; `Statics.re`'s
  `NOTE(yuchen)` documents a correctness caveat.
- **`Test_Statics_Sums`' `badTypeName`**, reported by an earlier scan — it is
  Hazel source inside a `{|...|}` literal, not OCaml.
- **Seven reported definitions were false positives the build caught.** Each
  became a suppression rule in the detector rather than a one-off exclusion.

## Two things that grew coverage instead of shrinking it

- `Test_Coverage`'s `nested_constructors_exhaustive` and
  `type_function_scrutinee` are complete tests that were never added to the suite
  list. Both pass; now registered (62 -> 64 in that suite).
- `Test_Evaluator_Properties`' `qcheck_preservation_test` was unreferenced
  because its registration was commented out with "Disabled due to known issues
  with preservation". It is now registered as an explicit `Alcotest.skip()` so the
  gap appears in the report instead of hiding as dead code.

## One deletion worth naming

**`VarBstMap`** — a 237-line module plus a 187-line `.rei` — is deleted entirely.
Its only reference in the whole repo was
`module M = { include VarBstMap.Ordered; };` inside a match arm of
`Test_Grammar.re`, where `M` is then never used: a no-op that made the module look
reachable. Flagging it because it is a documented, odoc-commented data structure,
not obviously junk. If anyone wants it kept as future API, this is the commit to
object to.

## Verification

`dune build @src/fmt src --profile release` — the gating CI build, where warnings
32/33/34/37 are errors — is clean. `make test-quick`: **3,268 passing**.

`make dead-code` reports **23** dead definitions in `src/`, not zero:

- **19** are the restorations above, kept at reviewer request.
- **3** arrived dead from the `dev` merge and are not this branch's to judge —
  `CLI/Run.re`'s `evaluate_with_probe_map`, `Refractors.persist`, and
  `Token.of_projector_invoke_opt`, all landed by the fast-parse work and not yet
  wired up.
- **1**, `TutorialGrading.percentage_view`, is removed by #2437's
  `include Grading;` dedup, one branch up the stack.

So the detector-zero claim from round 1 no longer holds, deliberately. Anyone
re-running the sweep should read the table above first.

title: Type-hole inference, integrated with dev (without the TPat-solving experiment)
body:
An alternative integration of the type-hole-inference work (PR #1872) with current `dev`, branched from commit `0b9d841ca9` instead of the #1872 tip. Per feedback from the original author, this **excludes the "tpats now use type provenances" experiment** (the commits from `65433eeb6f` onward), which had integrated TPat-as-provenance too deeply. Compare with #2290, which was based on the tip and carried that experiment through the elastatics merge.

## What this includes / excludes

- **Included:** Typ-level type-hole inference — annotated `type_provenance_t`, constraint-returning `Typ.meet`, the `Inference.solve` monolith, the `TypeHole` projector, and the inference pipeline wired end-to-end through dev's elastatics statics.
- **Excluded:** the TPat-solving experiment. `tpat_term` stays the conventional `Invalid | EmptyHole | MultiHole | Var` (matching dev), so there is **no** TPat-as-provenance, no `TypeSubstitution` provenance, and none of the deep TPat integration. The inference module stays the single `inference/inference.re` (not the experiment's `inference/` split).

Because the TPat grammar matches dev, the elastatics merge is dramatically cleaner than #2290: `Equality.re` and `Abbreviate.re` don't even conflict, and there are zero TPat-pattern rewrites.

## Commit sequence (for review)

1. `35a4dbf` — merge `dev` into the `0b9d841ca9` base (conflict resolution; build intentionally not green yet)
2. `71e8d0c` — post-merge build fixes: annotated-provenance threading, `Prov`/`equivalence` in TermBase, inference monolith adapted to dev's new sorts (`DrvQuoteTy`/`Projector`/`Sig`), `MatchedTyp` provenance patterns, inference wired into `mk_with_inference`/`CachedStatics`
3. `817db6c` — `dune fmt` + fix three `==`-against-fresh-provenance comparisons (bulk-rewrite artifact) to proper shape matches
4. `6c741cf` — bump CI test timeout 20m → 40m

## Resolution strategy

- **dev wholesale** for the elastatics-rewritten `Statics` / `Info` / `StaticsBase` / `CustomStatics` and the restructured test suite; deletions accepted for `Self` / `Elaborator` / `helpful-assistant` / `Test_Info` / `Test_Evaluator_Probe`.
- **Manual merge** of the term layer: kept the base's annotated `type_provenance_t`, constraint-returning `meet`, and `matched_*_of_prov` helpers; took dev's `Mod`/`Sig`/`MPat` sorts, `DrvQuoteTy`, and conventional `TPat`.
- **Glue** (`CachedStatics` / `CachedSyntax` / `ProjectorInfo` / `ProjectorView` / `CodeEditable` / CLI) threads the inference map (`Inference.SolutionMap`) and `sample_focus` through dev's structures.

## Inference wiring

`Info.exp`/`Info.pat` carry a `constraints` field. `Statics.add` records the subsumption equivalence `Con(ana, elab_syn_ty)` plus the structural constraints `Typ.meet` emits. `mk_with_inference` aggregates all Info constraints (deduped by representative id) and runs `Inference.solve`, returning the solution map that `CachedStatics` exposes and the TypeHole projector consumes. (Per-handler `MatchedTyp` constraint emission — the "quality improvements" from #2290 — is intentionally NOT carried here; `MatchedTyp` stays dev's 2-tuple form, and constraints flow via the core `meet`/subsumption path. Worth a follow-up if inference precision needs it.)

title: Escape sequence handling for string literals
body:
Previously, Hazel treated strings as purely literal sequences of characters without interpreting escape sequences (e.g. \n, \t, \\). This PR introduces support for escape sequences in standard strings, while adding a new Raw String literal construct (r"...") that ignores escape codes and preserves all characters verbatim, similar to how standard strings acted previously.

Closes #2379

title: Split the B2T2 slides per operation, in line with the current benchmark
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Needs a second opinion on one thing:** commit 1 switches `MenhirCorpus` from
> `Parser.to_zipper` to `Parser.to_segment`, and I am **not confident that is safe
> in general** — only that it holds across today's corpus. See
> "[The part I'm unsure about](#the-part-im-unsure-about)". The slide split
> (commit 2) is independent and can land without it.

## What

**Splits the B2T2 slides per operation, bringing them in line with the current
version of the benchmark.** The committed slides grouped several categories into
one file each — `Aggregate`, `Subtable`, `Properties`, `Ordering`,
`MissingValues`, `DataCleaning`, `AccessSubcomponents`, and the three Errors
"parts" — while the artifact's lab sources keep one file per operation. This
regenerates `hazel-programs/docs/b2t2` from those sources: **39 files → 62**, one
slide per operation, and picks up the upstream slide edits along with the split.

The menu therefore goes from 39 to 62 entries. That's the user-visible part of
this PR and the bit worth an opinion.

Names and menu order come from the manifest in `sync-slides.sh` (B2T2 operation
order, not alphabetical). The 28 slides that were already one-per-operation keep
their existing filenames, so the churn is limited to the 10 grouped files and the
33 replacing them.

## Why it also makes the suite much faster

The grouped files were the largest programs in the corpus — `table-api-aggregate.hz`
alone was 10.5 KB — and the editor parser is superlinear: `to_segment` only splits
at top-level boundaries, so within a segment cost still grows faster than linearly.
Re-splitting the same content (largest file now 6.7 KB, total bytes essentially
unchanged) cut `MarkerParse.of_text` over the corpus by **39%** and
`Parser.to_segment` by **32%**.

So this is faster while testing *more*: the suite gains 69 cases, because 62
slides generate more per-slide checks than 39 did.

| group | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `MenhirCorpus` | 90.4 s | 21.2 s |
| `DocSlides.ReparseBackuptext` | 52.7 s | 11.7 s |
| `TextRoundtrip.DocSlides` | 103.4 s | 78.0 s |
| **full suite (local)** | **345.5 s** | **211.0 s** (−38.9%) |
| test cases | 3496 | 3565 |

Measured locally with a `junit_alcotest` patched to record real per-case times —
upstream hardcodes `~time:0.`, which is why none of this was visible from the
existing reports.

## Commit 1: the test-side parse changes

Two changes, independent of the slide split:

**`MenhirCorpus` parses via `to_segment` instead of `to_zipper`** (90.4 s → 37.2 s
on the old corpus). See the warning below.

**`MenhirCorpus` and `DocSlides.ReparseBackuptext` share the parse.** They turn out
to check the same programs — the corpus files *are* the slide sources — and both
need the typing parser's segment, which each was paying for separately.
`test/ParsedCorpus.re` memoizes it, taking `ReparseBackuptext` from 51.7 s to
11.5 s. Making the cache hit required `MenhirCorpus` to normalize the way the load
path does (dedent every line, strip one trailing newline) rather than
`String.trim`, since otherwise the two callers key different strings for the same
program. That drops the indented-form differential — narrow, and a shape
production never produces, since every slide is dedented on load.

Worth recording that the original hypothesis here was wrong: the two *slide*
groups looked redundant, but `DocSlides` spends its time in `MarkerParse.of_text`
and `ReparseBackuptext` in `Parser.to_segment`, and the one call they share costs
about a tenth of a second. The real duplication was with `MenhirCorpus`.

## The part I'm unsure about

`Parser.to_zipper` is the **definitional** editor parse — it replays what the
editor does per keystroke. `Parser.to_segment` is an *optimization* over it: it
splits the input at points it believes are safe, strips the convex grout artifact
`Zipper.init()` leaves behind, then does a final top-level regrout to reconcile
shapes across boundaries. Any of those three steps could plausibly differ from
to_zipper for a program shape not in today's corpus.

**What I did verify**, because it's the failure mode that would hide itself:
`check_file` silently passes when the editor parser returns `None`, so a file that
`to_segment` rejected would have dropped out of coverage with the suite still
green. That does not happen — across all corpus files both entry points accept
every file and produce structurally equal terms.

**What I did not verify** is that the two agree in general. The consequence is
that `MenhirCorpus` now pins menhir against the optimized parser rather than the
ground-truth one, so if `to_segment` ever drifts from `to_zipper`, this test would
compare against the wrong baseline and not notice.

The invariant "`to_segment` ≡ `to_zipper` corpus-wide" is worth asserting, but
doing so costs about what using `to_zipper` here would, which is the entire saving
— so it belongs in a periodic run rather than per-PR. That's noted in the file's
header. **If reviewers would rather not take this on faith, commit 1's swap can be
dropped and the shared-parse half kept; the slide split carries most of the win
regardless.**

## `known_gaps` fallout, which is an improvement

The single `table-api-properties.hz` gap entry was tolerating three operations at
once. Split, the `[()]` tokenizer quirk turns out to affect `header` and `ncols`
but **not** `nrows` — so the ledger now names the two files that actually carry it,
and `nrows` is genuinely checked for the first time. No new gaps.

## Verified

- `make dev` builds the web bundle against the regenerated `Slides.re`
- full suite green
- `MenhirCorpus` green with the re-attributed ledger

## Not addressed here

`TextRoundtrip.DocSlides` is now the largest remaining group at 78 s, all of it in
`MarkerParse.of_text` → `to_zipper`. Reimplementing that over `to_segment` is worth
roughly 40 s more, but it is production code (`PersistentZipper`'s fallback path),
needs a zipper rather than a segment, and also strips implicit holes and preserves
refractors — a real refactor rather than a substitution, so it is deliberately out
of scope.

Separately: the `unused open EditingPrelude` warning in `Test_ReparseDocSlides.re`
is untouched here. Its removal belongs to #2456, on #2422.

title: Improved Unicode support
body:
This extends and improves Hazel's unicode support, both the editor and the language, permitting unicode use in identifiers (user facing) and in arbitrary delimiters, as well as fixing bugs and inconsistencies around unicode use in comments and quoted tuple levels

Previously non-ASCII chars like emojis only really worked inside string literals. Comments, quoted labels and operator tokens could technically hold them but were buggy because width handling was gated on `is_string`: `#😀#` measured one column narrower than it rendered, shifting carets, selections and click-mapping for the rest of the row. Non-paste insertion of non-unicode characters was impossible anywhere, because `Insert` key handling gated on single-byte length, so any multi-byte entry silently produced no insert.

**Identifiers take Unicode**, so `café`, `日本語` and `x😀` lex as one tile. Constructors are still distinguished by capitalization, with caseless characters counting as non-uppercase: `😀foo` is a variable, `Foo😀` a constructor.

**Operators are now defined positively.** They were previously whatever was left over after excluding names, whitespace and delimiters; technically on dev now loose pasted emoji become operators without anyone having decided that. Now: the 18 ASCII characters already in use, plus the five the language actually uses in operator position (`∈ ≠ ≮ ≯ ⊆`, display-only, emitted by `ExpToSegment` for derivation operators). Identifiers are now the complement, so the two remain disjoint by construction.

**Hazel's string builtins now use grapheme indexing**. `string_search` returns an index that composes with `string_sub` and is bounded by `string_length`; these agreed before only by all being bytes. `string_length("😀")` was 4.

Also fixed: truncation in `Abbreviate`/`ProbeText` cutting mid-cluster; CLI type error message code indexing columns as bytes being wrong in the presence of unicode, `wrap_quote`/`wrap_balanced` wrapping a whole token when only part of it was selected.

`ocamllex` has no Unicode properties, so the text lexer admits well-formed UTF-8 in names minus the whitelist, which is a superset of the editor's rule. The `MakeTerm`/Menhir equivalence properties now generate non-ASCII identifiers and string literals. Note:  the Unicode operator whitelist is hand-maintained in both `Token.re` and `Lexer.mll` with no compile-time link.

**Invisible characters render as labeled cells, and pasted code is NFC-normalized.** With names the complement of operators, every invisible format character (zero-width space, bidi controls, soft hyphen, …) became a valid name character: `ba​r` with a hidden ZWSP looks identical to `bar` but is a different variable, and measured one column wider than it rendered. A cluster consisting only of such codepoints now draws as a small hex-labeled box with a tooltip, restoring measurement/render agreement (attached forms like an emoji's VS16 are untouched). `unicode-bidi: isolate` on tokens keeps RTL text or a stray direction override in one token from visually reordering its neighbors. Pasted and agent-introduced code is NFC-normalized outside string literals — macOS paste sources emit decomposed accents, so a pasted `café` otherwise never matches a typed one — while literal contents are preserved byte-for-byte (per UTS #55, which recommends exactly this editor/language split; a fuller options survey lives in local plans/unicode-due-diligence.md).

title: Add Cut/Copy/Paste to the editor context menu
body:
## Summary

Adds a clipboard section (Cut / Copy / Paste) to the editor's right-click context menu, with platform-appropriate shortcut chips (⌘X/⌘C/⌘V on Mac, Ctrl+X/C/V elsewhere).

- **Cut / Copy** are grayed out when the selection is empty. They write the system clipboard using the same helpers as the existing Cmd/Ctrl+C/X keyboard path (including the segment-cache fast-paste optimization), which were hoisted out of the key handler so both paths share them.
- **Paste** is always available. ~~Menu items carry an `Action.t` payload, so the menu's Paste uses a placeholder `Paste("")`; the new `perform_from_menu` inject intercepts it, reads the system clipboard asynchronously, and dispatches the real `Paste(text)` when it arrives, closing the menu immediately.~~
  **Revised** ([review](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/pull/2341#discussion_r3476994230)): rows carry `ContextMenu.command = Perform(Action.t) | PasteFromClipboard` instead of a bare `Action.t`, so no placeholder action exists at all. `action_item` wraps its argument in `Perform` — every row builder is unchanged — and the Paste row carries `PasteFromClipboard`, which `perform_from_menu` turns into the real `Paste(text)` once the async clipboard read lands, closing the menu immediately.
  Paste is never grayed out, because the web can't report whether the clipboard is empty short of reading it, and that read is permission-gated and async (Chrome prompts once per origin, Firefox and Safari on every read) — testing it on menu-open would prompt on every right-click. Google Docs and VS Code for the Web leave Paste enabled for the same reason and find out at click time.
- **Right-click now preserves selections.** Previously right-click always dispatched `Move(Point(...))`, collapsing the selection before the menu opened — which would have made Copy useless. A new `click_in_selection` hit test keeps the selection when the click lands inside its measured extent; clicks outside still move the caret as before.
- Added `.disabled` styling for context-menu rows (dimmed, no hover highlight) and bumped the menu height estimate used for open-direction flipping, since the menu gained three permanent rows.

Known approximation: the hit test uses the selection's first/last piece measurements, so for char-level selections that split a token the "inside" region can be slightly wider than the highlighted text.

## Testing

- `make dev` builds clean.
- Manual: select code → right-click inside the selection → Cut/Copy act on it; right-click elsewhere → caret moves, Cut/Copy disabled, Paste inserts clipboard contents. Keyboard menu navigation (arrows/Enter) drives the same actions.
- The `command`-type revision above still wants a manual re-check — same flows, different dispatch path.
